    "question": "Seller delivered the goods ordered by Buyer under FCA Carrier. Buyer was notified that the goods arrived and ready for unloading. The goods were damaged during the unloading from seller's truck. Who bears the risk?",
    "choices": {
      "A": "Seller",
      "B": "Terminal operator",
      "C": "Buyer",
      "D": "Carrier"
    },
    "correct": "C",
    "reason": "Under FCA, risk transfers when goods are delivered to the carrier. Unloading at destination is the buyer's risk."
  },
  "42": {
    "question": "Under FAS, which cost is the buyer's responsibility?",
    "choices": {
      "A": "Export customs clearance",
      "B": "Terminal Handling Charge before placing goods alongside ship",
      "C": "Loading the goods onto the vessel",
      "D": "Inland transport to the port of shipment"
    },
    "correct": "C",
    "reason": "Under FAS, the seller is responsible for export customs clearance and placing the goods alongside the nominated vessel. Once alongside, the buyer becomes responsible for loading the goods onto the vessel and everything thereafter (main carriage, insurance, unloading, import clearance)."
  },
  "43": {
    "question": "Goods are shipped under FOB. The seller loads the goods onboard, but the crane operator drops the container during loading. Who bears the loss?",
    "choices": {
      "A": "Seller",
      "B": "Terminal operator",
      "C": "Buyer",
      "D": "Carrier"
    },
    "correct": "A",
    "reason": "Under FOB, risk transfers only once goods are actually loaded on board the vessel. Damage during the loading process, before on-board status is achieved, remains the seller's risk."
  },
  "44": {
    "question": "Under CFR, the seller pays ocean freight. The goods are damaged during the voyage. Who bears the risk?",
    "choices": {
      "A": "Seller, because freight was prepaid",
      "B": "Buyer, because risk transferred at shipment",
      "C": "Carrier",
      "D": "Insurance company"
    },
    "correct": "B",
    "reason": "Under CFR, risk transfers to the buyer once goods are loaded on board the vessel, despite the seller paying freight."
  },
  "45": {
    "question": "Under FOB, seller delivers early, but vessel not yet arrived. Goods are damaged while waiting. Risk lies with:",
    "choices": {
      "A": "Seller",
      "B": "Carrier",
      "C": "Buyer",
      "D": "Port authority"
    },
    "correct": "A",
    "reason": "Under FOB, risk transfers only when goods are loaded on board the vessel. Until then, the seller bears the risk."
  },
  "46": {
    "question": "Goods are sold under DAP Buyer's Warehouse. The truck arrives ready for unloading but the buyer refuses the unloading due to labor issues. Who bears the risk at that moment?",
    "choices": {
      "A": "Seller",
      "B": "Carrier",
      "C": "Buyer",
      "D": "Customs authority"
    },
    "correct": "C",
    "reason": "Under DAP, risk transfers when goods are placed at the buyer's disposal at the named destination. Refusal to accept means the buyer bears the risk."
  },
  "47": {
    "question": "Seller and buyer agreed on EXW Seller's Factory. The seller loads the goods onto the buyer's truck as a favor, and damage occurs during loading. Who bears the risk?",
    "choices": {
      "A": "Seller",
      "B": "Carrier",
      "C": "Buyer",
      "D": "Insurance company"
    },
    "correct": "C",
    "reason": "Under EXW, risk transfers when goods are made available at the seller's premises. Loading by the seller as a favor does not change the risk transfer point."
  },
  "48": {
    "question": "Under FCA, goods are delivered at the seller's premises. When does risk transfer?",
    "choices": {
      "A": "After export clearance",
      "B": "When goods are loaded on buyer's carrier",
      "C": "Upon arrival at port",
      "D": "When freight is paid"
    },
    "correct": "B",
    "reason": "Under FCA at the seller's premises, risk transfers when the goods are loaded on the buyer's collecting vehicle."
  },
  "49": {
    "question": "Which Incoterm places maximum obligation on the seller?",
    "choices": {
      "A": "DAP",
      "B": "DDP",
      "C": "DPU",
      "D": "CIF"
    },
    "correct": "B",
    "reason": "DDP places the maximum obligation on the seller, covering all costs, risks, and import clearance to the buyer's premises."
  },
  "50": {
    "question": "Goods are shipped under CPT. The seller paid freight, but the goods were lost after being handed to the first carrier. Who bears the loss?",
    "choices": {
      "A": "Seller",
      "B": "Carrier",
      "C": "Buyer",
      "D": "Insurance company"
    },
    "correct": "C",
    "reason": "Under CPT, risk transfers to the buyer when goods are handed to the first carrier. The buyer bears the loss despite the seller paying freight."
  },
  "51": {
    "question": "Which Incoterm can be used for any mode of transport, including multimodal?",
    "choices": {
      "A": "FOB",
      "B": "FCA",
      "C": "CFR",
      "D": "FAS"
    },
    "correct": "B",
    "reason": "FCA is a multimodal Incoterm suitable for any mode of transport, including multimodal."
  },
  "52": {
    "question": "Under DPU, delivery is agreed at a terminal without unloading equipment. What is the implication?",
    "choices": {
      "A": "Buyer must unload",
      "B": "Seller bears the risk of unloading",
      "C": "Contract is invalid",
      "D": "Risk transfers before unloading"
    },
    "correct": "B",
    "reason": "Under DPU, the seller bears the risk of unloading the goods at the named place of destination."
  },
  "53": {
    "question": "Which Incoterm is incorrectly paired with its transport mode?",
    "choices": {
      "A": "CIF – Sea transport",
      "B": "DAP – Any mode",
      "C": "FOB – Sea transport",
      "D": "FAS – Air transport"
    },
    "correct": "D",
    "reason": "FAS is for sea/inland waterway transport only, not air transport."
  },
  "54": {
    "question": "Under CPT, which statement is TRUE?",
    "choices": {
      "A": "Risk transfers at destination",
      "B": "Seller bears risk during carriage",
      "C": "Risk transfers when goods are handed to first carrier",
      "D": "Seller must insure the goods"
    },
    "correct": "C",
    "reason": "Under CPT, risk transfers when the goods are handed to the first carrier."
  },
  "55": {
    "question": "Which Incoterm requires the seller to deliver goods on board the vessel?",
    "choices": {
      "A": "FCA",
      "B": "FAS",
      "C": "FOB",
      "D": "DPU"
    },
    "correct": "C",
    "reason": "FOB requires the seller to deliver goods on board the vessel at the named port of shipment."
  },
  "56": {
    "question": "Which Incoterm is most suitable when the seller can handle both export and import clearance?",
    "choices": {
      "A": "DAP",
      "B": "DDP",
      "C": "DPU",
      "D": "CIF"
    },
    "correct": "B",
    "reason": "DDP requires the seller to handle both export and import clearance, making it suitable for sellers capable of doing both."
  },
  "57": {
    "question": "Under DAP, risk transfers:",
    "choices": {
      "A": "At shipment",
      "B": "After unloading",
      "C": "Upon arrival, ready for unloading",
      "D": "After import clearance"
    },
    "correct": "C",
    "reason": "Under DAP, risk transfers when the goods are placed at the disposal of the buyer at the named destination, ready for unloading."
  },
  "58": {
    "question": "Under DPU, import duties are paid by:",
    "choices": {
      "A": "Seller",
      "B": "Carrier",
      "C": "Buyer",
      "D": "Port authority"
    },
    "correct": "C",
    "reason": "Under DPU, the buyer is responsible for import duties and taxes."
  },
  "59": {
    "question": "In the application of Method Four in determining customs value if neither the imported goods nor identical nor similar imported goods are sold in the Philippines in the condition as imported the dutiable value shall be based on the unit price at which the imported goods, after further processing. At whose instance may such be done?",
    "choices": {
      "A": "District Collector",
      "B": "District Collector subject to approval of the Commissioner",
      "C": "Deputy Commissioner, AOCG",
      "D": "Importer"
    },
    "correct": "D",
    "reason": "Under Method Four (Deductive Value), the importer may request valuation based on further processing, as provided under CMTA."
  },
  "60": {
    "question": "Imported goods shall be valued in accordance with the provisions of Section 701 of CMTA whenever the conditions prescribed therein are fulfilled. What is the valuation method under Section 701?",
    "choices": {
      "A": "Method One",
      "B": "Method Two",
      "C": "Method Three",
      "D": "Method Four"
    },
    "correct": "A",
    "reason": "Section 701 of the CMTA covers Method One - Transaction Value."
  },
  "61": {
    "question": "What is a condition before all additions or adjustments to the price actually paid or payable be made?",
    "choices": {
      "A": "All additions must be based on the decision of the Bureau of Customs",
      "B": "All additions must be based only on the basis of objective and quantifiable data",
      "C": "All additions must be based on the agreement between the importer and the Bureau of Customs",
      "D": "All of the above"
    },
    "correct": "B",
    "reason": "Additions to the price actually paid or payable must be based on objective and quantifiable data, as required under WTO Valuation Agreement."
  },
  "62": {
    "question": "Where the customs value cannot be determined under the provisions of Section 701, it is to be determined by proceeding sequentially through Section 702, 703, 704, 705, and 706. What is the exception to the valuation sequential rule?",
    "choices": {
      "A": "Application of Method Four from Method Two",
      "B": "Application of Method Five from Method Three",
      "C": "Application of Method Six from Method Four",
      "D": "None of the choices"
    },
    "correct": "D",
    "reason": "Under CMTA Section 700, the actual exception allows the importer to request that Method Five (Computed Value, Sec. 705) be applied before Method Four (Deductive Value, Sec. 704). None of choices A-C correctly describe this swap, so the answer is None of the choices."
  },
  "63": {
    "question": "Who may request for an exception to the application of the valuation sequential rule?",
    "choices": {
      "A": "Customs Appraiser",
      "B": "District Collector",
      "C": "Importer",
      "D": "Any of the above"
    },
    "correct": "C",
    "reason": "Only the importer may request an exception to the sequential application of valuation methods, as provided under the WTO Valuation Agreement."
  },
  "64": {
    "question": "If the dutiable value cannot be determined under Method One to Method Five it shall be determined by using other reasonable means and on the basis of data available in which of the following places?",
    "choices": {
      "A": "Port of entry",
      "B": "Philippines",
      "C": "Country of exportation",
      "D": "Any of the choices"
    },
    "correct": "B",
    "reason": "Method Six (Fallback Method) values are determined using reasonable means consistent with the Agreement's principles, based on data available in the country of importation — i.e., the Philippines — not on data from any location generally."
  },
  "65": {
    "question": "What is the valuation method under CMTA, Section 705?",
    "choices": {
      "A": "Method Two",
      "B": "Method Three",
      "C": "Method Four",
      "D": "Method Five"
    },
    "correct": "D",
    "reason": "Section 705 of the CMTA covers Method Five - Computed Value."
  },
  "66": {
    "question": "Which of the following is a valid basis in determining dutiable value under Method Six?",
    "choices": {
      "A": "The selling price in the Philippines of goods produced in the Philippines",
      "B": "System that provides for the acceptance for customs purposes of the higher of two alternative values",
      "C": "The price of goods in the domestic market of the country of exportation",
      "D": "All of the above are contrary to the WTO Valuation Agreement in determining dutiable value"
    },
    "correct": "D",
    "reason": "Method Six (Fallback Method) cannot use domestic sales prices, minimum values, or arbitrary systems; all the listed options are prohibited under the WTO Valuation Agreement."
  },
  "67": {
    "question": "If the proper person requests for an exception to the application of the valuation sequential rule and still the customs value cannot be determined, what is the proper method of valuation to be applied?",
    "choices": {
      "A": "Method Two",
      "B": "Method Three",
      "C": "Method Four",
      "D": "Method Five"
    },
    "correct": "C",
    "reason": "If the importer's request to use Method Five (Computed Value) ahead of Method Four fails to yield a value, the customs value shall then be determined under Method Four (Deductive Value), per CMTA Section 700."
  },
  "68": {
    "question": "For purposes of computing dutiable value under the provisions of Section 701 Method One which of the following is an acceptable restriction imposed by the seller with regard to the disposition or use of the goods by the buyer?",
    "choices": {
      "A": "Restriction imposed as required by law",
      "B": "Restriction that limit the geographical area in which the goods may be resold",
      "C": "Restriction that does not substantially affect the value of the goods",
      "D": "All of the above are acceptable restrictions"
    },
    "correct": "D",
    "reason": "Acceptable restrictions include those imposed by law, limitations on geographical resale, and restrictions that do not substantially affect the value of the goods."
  },
  "69": {
    "question": "The deductive value which shall be based on the unit price at which the imported goods or identical or similar imported goods are sold in the Philippines, in the same condition as when imported, in the greatest aggregate quantity, at or about the time of the importation of the goods being valued to persons not related to the persons from whom they buy such goods. Who is the seller and buyer referred to in the definition?",
    "choices": {
      "A": "The seller refers to the foreign supplier while the buyer refers to the importer",
      "B": "The seller refers to the importer of the goods being valued and the buyer is the local buyer who should not be related to the seller.",
      "C": "The seller refers to the local supplier and the buyer refers to the importer",
      "D": "Any of the situation applies"
    },
    "correct": "B",
    "reason": "In Method Four, the seller is the importer of the goods being valued, and the buyer is the local buyer who must be unrelated to the seller."
  },
  "70": {
    "question": "What is the condition before any amount of royalties and license fees related to the goods being valued shall be considered as an addition to the price actually paid or payable for purposes of computing dutiable value?",
    "choices": {
      "A": "The buyer must not be related to the seller",
      "B": "The seller must not be related to the buyer in any manner",
      "C": "The buyer pays the royalty either directly or indirectly as a condition of sale of the goods",
      "D": "All of the above are the conditions"
    },
    "correct": "C",
    "reason": "Royalties and license fees are added to the price actually paid or payable only if the buyer pays them as a condition of sale of the goods, regardless of relationship between parties."
  },
  "71": {
    "question": "Which of the following is a valid basis in determining dutiable value under Method Six?",
    "choices": {
      "A": "The price of goods in the domestic market of the country of exportation",
      "B": "The price of goods for export to a country other than the Philippines",
      "C": "Minimum customs values",
      "D": "All of the choices are not valid basis in determining dutiable value under Method Six"
    },
    "correct": "D",
    "reason": "Method Six (Fallback Method) cannot use domestic sales prices, export prices to other countries, or minimum values as valid bases."
  },
  "72": {
    "question": "Identical goods refer to goods which are the same in all respects, including physical characteristics, quality and reputation, although minor differences in appearance do not preclude goods from being regarded as identical. A shipment of white electric fans and a shipment of red electric fans are otherwise the same brand, model, specifications, and quality. Can the red electric fans be treated as 'identical goods' to the white ones for customs valuation purposes?",
    "choices": {
      "A": "No, because any physical difference, including color, disqualifies them from being identical",
      "B": "Yes, because color is a minor difference in appearance that does not preclude an identical goods classification",
      "C": "No, but they can still be treated as similar goods instead",
      "D": "It depends on whether the Bureau of Customs specifically approves the classification"
    },
    "correct": "B",
    "reason": "Under the CMTA and the WTO Valuation Agreement, 'identical goods' are goods that are the same in all respects, but minor differences in appearance — such as color — do not preclude goods from being regarded as identical, provided they otherwise conform to the definition."
  },
  "73": {
    "question": "When a goods declaration is presented to the Bureau of Customs and the concerned customs officer has reason to doubt the truth or accuracy of the declaration or of the documents attached therein what may be done by the Bureau?",
    "choices": {
      "A": "The Bureau of Customs may ask the importer to provide further explanation that the entered value represents an accurate transaction value",
      "B": "The Bureau of Customs may ask the importer to produce additional documents to prove that the entered transaction value is accurate",
      "C": "The Bureau of Customs may ask the importer to produce any other evidence to prove that the entered transaction value is accurate",
      "D": "Any of the above may be done by the Bureau of Customs."
    },
    "correct": "D",
    "reason": "The BOC may request further explanation, additional documents, or any other evidence to verify the accuracy of the declared value."
  },
  "74": {
    "question": "Where the dutiable value cannot be determined under Method Four the dutiable value shall be the computed value of the sum of different cost elements. Which of the following is not among those cost elements?",
    "choices": {
      "A": "The cost or the value of materials and fabrication or other processing employed in producing the imported goods",
      "B": "The amount for profit and general expenses equal to that usually reflected in the sale of goods of the same class or kind as the goods being valued which are made by producers in the country of exportation for export to the Philippines.",
      "C": "The freight, insurance fees and other transportation expenses for the importation of the goods",
      "D": "All of the above are proper cost elements"
    },
    "correct": "C",
    "reason": "Freight, insurance, and transportation expenses are not part of Method Five (Computed Value); they are added separately."
  },
  "75": {
    "question": "In applying Section 702-Transaction Value of Identical Goods or Section 703 Transaction Value of Similar goods, if more than one transaction value of identical goods or similar goods are found, what rule shall be applied?",
    "choices": {
      "A": "Whichever is the highest rule applies",
      "B": "Whichever is the latest rule applies",
      "C": "Whichever is the lowest rule applies",
      "D": "Any of the above is correct applies"
    },
    "correct": "C",
    "reason": "When multiple transaction values of identical or similar goods are found, the lowest value shall be applied."
  },
  "76": {
    "question": "In determining the dutiable value using Method One Transaction value, there are cost elements that shall be added to the price actually paid or payable for the imported goods. What is a condition before a cost element may be a positive adjustment to the price actually paid or payable?",
    "choices": {
      "A": "To the extent that the cost element is incurred by both the seller and buyer and payable at a future date",
      "B": "To the extent that the cost element is incurred by seller and already included in the price actually paid or payable.",
      "C": "To the extent that the cost element is incurred by the buyer and not included in the price actually paid or payable.",
      "D": "None of the choices"
    },
    "correct": "C",
    "reason": "An adjustment is added only if the cost is incurred by the buyer and not already included in the price actually paid or payable."
  },
  "77": {
    "question": "For the assessment and collection of import duty upon imported goods and for other purposes, the value and prices thereof quoted in foreign currency shall be converted into the currency of the Philippines at the current rate of exchange or value specified or published, from time to time. Which of the following agencies should publish the rate of exchange?",
    "choices": {
      "A": "PSA",
      "B": "BSP",
      "C": "NEDA",
      "D": "BOC"
    },
    "correct": "B",
    "reason": "The Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP) publishes the official rate of exchange for customs valuation purposes."
  },
  "78": {
    "question": "In the application of Method Four if neither the imported goods nor identical nor similar imported goods are sold at or about the time of importation of the goods being valued in the Philippines in the conditions they were imported, the customs value shall be based on the unit price at which the imported goods or identical or similar imported goods sold in the Philippines in the condition they were imported and at the earliest date after the importation of the goods being valued. What is the time frame provided under CMTA?",
    "choices": {
      "A": "Before the expiration of thirty (30) days after such importation",
      "B": "Before the expiration of forty five (45) days after such importation",
      "C": "Before the expiration of sixty (60) days after such importation",
      "D": "Before the expiration of ninety (90) days after such importation"
    },
    "correct": "D",
    "reason": "Under CMTA, the earliest date after importation for Method Four is before the expiration of ninety (90) days."
  },
  "79": {
    "question": "In determining dutiable value using Method One are engineering, development, artwork, design work and plans and sketches undertaken in the Philippines and necessary for the production of imported goods, where such goods are supplied directly or indirectly by the buyer free of charge or at a reduced cost for use in connection with the production and sale for export of the imported goods considered as assist?",
    "choices": {
      "A": "Yes, but use of Method One is not precluded",
      "B": "No, but use of Method One is precluded.",
      "C": "Yes, but use of Method One is precluded",
      "D": "No, but use of Method One is not precluded"
    },
    "correct": "D",
    "reason": "Engineering, design work, and similar work undertaken in the Philippines (the country of importation) is explicitly excluded from being treated as an assist. Since it is not an assist, no addition is required, and the use of Method One is not precluded."
  },
  "80": {
    "question": "If in the course of determining the dutiable value of imported goods, it becomes necessary to delay the final determination of such dutiable value, how may the importer effect release of imported goods?",
    "choices": {
      "A": "There is nothing that can be done by the importer but to pay duties and taxes to avoid delay in the release of imported goods",
      "B": "Release of imported goods under tentative assessment upon posting of sufficient security equal to the duties and taxes due on the imported goods",
      "C": "Release of imported goods under tentative assessment upon posting of sufficient security",
      "D": "Any of the above"
    },
    "correct": "C",
    "reason": "The importer may secure release under tentative assessment upon posting of sufficient security."
  },
  "81": {
    "question": "Which of the following is not a proper term in the statement that 'similar goods' are goods which, although not alike in all respects, have like characteristics and similar component materials which enable them to perform the same functions and to be interchangeable, commercially",
    "choices": {
      "A": "Similar",
      "B": "Interchangeable",
      "C": "Same function",
      "D": "The statement is correct in all aspects."
    },
    "correct": "D",
    "reason": "The statement is correct in all aspects; all terms are proper in describing similar goods."
  },
  "82": {
    "question": "If the dutiable value of imported goods cannot be determined using Method Two and Method Three, what may be done by the importer if he does not want to apply the succeeding valuation method?",
    "choices": {
      "A": "The importer may request that Method One be used in the valuation of the imported goods.",
      "B": "The importer may request that customs value be determined using Computed Value.",
      "C": "The importer may request that customs value be determined using Deductive Value.",
      "D": "None of the choices"
    },
    "correct": "B",
    "reason": "If Methods Two and Three fail, the importer may request that the customs value be determined using Computed Value (Method Five)."
  },
  "83": {
    "question": "What is the main condition for the use of Method One?",
    "choices": {
      "A": "Conditions prescribed are fulfilled.",
      "B": "Carrying vessel has arrived.",
      "C": "Imported goods have been discharged from carrying vessel.",
      "D": "All of the above."
    },
    "correct": "A",
    "reason": "The main condition for the use of Method One is that the conditions prescribed in Section 701 are fulfilled."
  },
  "84": {
    "question": "In determining the dutiable value using Section 701 Transaction Value commissions and brokerage fees are to be added to the price actually paid or payable. Which of the following is not the commission contemplated under the law?",
    "choices": {
      "A": "Selling commission",
      "B": "Brokerage fees",
      "C": "Buying commission",
      "D": "All of the above are adjustments to the price actually paid or payable"
    },
    "correct": "C",
    "reason": "Buying commission is not added to the price actually paid or payable; only selling commissions and brokerage fees are added."
  },
  "85": {
    "question": "In determining customs value using Method Five may the Bureau of Customs require or compel any person not residing in the Philippines to produce for examination, or to allow access to, any account or other record for the purpose of determining a computed value?",
    "choices": {
      "A": "Yes, provided that the request is done through proper diplomatic channels.",
      "B": "Yes, provided that the importer agrees.",
      "C": "Yes, provided that the Secretary of Finance approves such request.",
      "D": "No"
    },
    "correct": "D",
    "reason": "The BOC cannot compel persons not residing in the Philippines to produce records for Method Five determination."
  },
  "86": {
    "question": "Which of the following is not a test value for purposes of determining whether in a sale between related parties the transaction value shall be accepted as the dutiable value?",
    "choices": {
      "A": "The transaction value in sales to unrelated buyers of identical or similar goods for export to the Philippines.",
      "B": "The Deductive Value of identical or similar goods.",
      "C": "The Computed Value of identical or similar goods.",
      "D": "None of the choices."
    },
    "correct": "D",
    "reason": "All the listed values are test values for determining acceptability of transaction value between related parties."
  },
  "87": {
    "question": "Which of the following is not relationship in the context of WTO Valuation Agreement?",
    "choices": {
      "A": "Together Buyer and Seller directly or indirectly control a third person",
      "B": "Both the Buyer and Seller are directly or indirectly controlled by a third person",
      "C": "Buyer and Seller are second cousins",
      "D": "All are considered as relationship under WVA"
    },
    "correct": "C",
    "reason": "The WTO Valuation Agreement's definition of 'related persons' enumerates specific family relationships (spouse, parent-child, siblings, grandparent-grandchild, uncle/aunt-nephew/niece, in-laws), which does not include cousins. 'Second cousins' therefore falls outside the defined relationship categories."
  },
  "88": {
    "question": "Choose the item which may not be considered as adjustment to the price actually paid or payable",
    "choices": {
      "A": "Cost of design done in the Philippines",
      "B": "Cost of containers",
      "C": "Selling commission",
      "D": "All of the above are adjustments to the price actually paid or payable"
    },
    "correct": "A",
    "reason": "Cost of design done in the Philippines is considered an assist but is not an adjustment to the price actually paid or payable."
  },
  "89": {
    "question": "In computing for Deductive Value which of the following should not be deducted from the unit price at which the imported goods or identical or similar goods are sold in the Philippines?",
    "choices": {
      "A": "Commissions usually paid or agreed to be paid and general expenses in connection with the sales in the Philippines of imported goods of the same class or kind",
      "B": "The usual costs of transport and insurance associated costs incurred within the Philippines.",
      "C": "The transport, insurance fees and other transportation expenses for the importations of the goods",
      "D": "All of the above are considered as deductions."
    },
    "correct": "C",
    "reason": "Transport, insurance, and transportation expenses for importation are not deducted in Method Four; they are added before valuation."
  },
  "90": {
    "question": "Which of the following may be considered as Transaction Value?",
    "choices": {
      "A": "Purchase price on FOB Singapore basis",
      "B": "Purchase price on CFR Manila basis",
      "C": "Purchase price on CIF Cebu basis",
      "D": "All of the above"
    },
    "correct": "D",
    "reason": "Transaction value may be based on any sale basis as long as it represents the price actually paid or payable for the goods."
  },
  "91": {
    "question": "There is no publication of exchange rate on a Good Friday. What shall be the applicable exchange rate for that day?",
    "choices": {
      "A": "Rate that shall be published following Monday",
      "B": "Rate published Thursday before Good Friday",
      "C": "Rate published Friday before Holy Week",
      "D": "None of the choices"
    },
    "correct": "B",
    "reason": "When no rate is published on a holiday, the rate published on the last working day before the holiday (Thursday) applies."
  },
  "92": {
    "question": "The GAAP applicable in case of Method Five.",
    "choices": {
      "A": "GAAP as determined by the Bureau of Customs.",
      "B": "GAAP in the Philippines.",
      "C": "GAAP in the exporting country.",
      "D": "GAAP as chosen by the importer."
    },
    "correct": "C",
    "reason": "In Method Five (Computed Value), the GAAP of the exporting country shall be used."
  },
  "93": {
    "question": "A Filipino importer provided assist in the form of design which was procured from a French designer based in Germany. What GAAP shall be used to value the assist?",
    "choices": {
      "A": "None as design is an intangible and therefore not considered as mandatory addition. As a rule intangibles are not subject to payment of customs duty.",
      "B": "GAAP in France as the designer is a French national.",
      "C": "GAAP in Germany the place where the design was made.",
      "D": "GAAP in the Philippines which is the importing country."
    },
    "correct": "C",
    "reason": "The assist (design) shall be valued using GAAP in the country where the design was produced (Germany)."
  },
  "94": {
    "question": "The transaction value of the imported goods is based on PAPP for those goods when sold for export to the Philippines. What shall be the tax treatment when there is sale by a free zone locator to the customs territory for consumption?",
    "choices": {
      "A": "The transaction value between the free zone and buyer in the customs territory shall be used.",
      "B": "The transaction value is not applicable as the sale is within the Philippines.",
      "C": "The transaction value of the raw materials when admitted into the free zone.",
      "D": "The transaction value as determined by the Import Assessment Service (IAS)."
    },
    "correct": "A",
    "reason": "When goods are withdrawn from a free zone into the customs territory, the transaction value between the free zone locator and the buyer in the customs territory shall be used."
  },
  "95": {
    "question": "Is there sale for export for time charter transaction between a ship owner and a domestic vessel operator?",
    "choices": {
      "A": "Yes, as there is outflow of foreign exchange in the transaction.",
      "B": "No, as the title of ownership of the vessel remains with the ship owner.",
      "C": "No, as the vessel will not be engaged in foreign trade.",
      "D": "Yes, as the vessel will travel from a foreign port to a Philippine port."
    },
    "correct": "B",
    "reason": "In a time charter, ownership of the vessel remains with the ship owner; therefore, there is no sale for export."
  },
  "96": {
    "question": "Filipino importer supplied used capital equipment as an assist to a foreign supplier. The capital equipment was previously imported from Germany brand new. How shall the equipment be valued?",
    "choices": {
      "A": "TV when the capital equipment was imported by the Filipino importer.",
      "B": "Total cost of the capital equipment.",
      "C": "Total cost of the equipment minus depreciation.",
      "D": "TV of the capital equipment as determined by the customs authorities of foreign supplier."
    },
    "correct": "C",
    "reason": "Used capital equipment supplied as an assist shall be valued at its total cost minus depreciation."
  },
  "97": {
    "question": "Is letter of credit amount always equal to the price actually paid or payable?",
    "choices": {
      "A": "Yes, as the amount in the letter of credit represents the agreed price between the buyer and the seller.",
      "B": "Not necessarily always.",
      "C": "No, because mandatory adjustments have to be considered.",
      "D": "None of the choices."
    },
    "correct": "C",
    "reason": "The LC amount is not always equal to the price actually paid or payable because mandatory adjustments (commissions, assists, etc.) must be added."
  },
  "98": {
    "question": "In a Free Carrier (FCA) delivery to a third person which of the following is to be considered as an Adjustment to the PAPP?",
    "choices": {
      "A": "Inland transport cost from seller's place to the delivery point.",
      "B": "Export customs clearance.",
      "C": "Unloading cost incurred at the place of delivery.",
      "D": "Inland marine to cover risk from supplier's place to place of delivery."
    },
    "correct": "A",
    "reason": "Inland transport cost from seller's place to the delivery point is an adjustment to the PAPP in FCA transactions."
  },
  "99": {
    "question": "Which of the following cost elements is not an Adjustment to the PAPP in a FCA transaction where the place of delivery is the supplier's factory:",
    "choices": {
      "A": "Cost of loading to the collecting vehicle.",
      "B": "Inland transport cost at the country of exportation.",
      "C": "Inland marine at the country of exportation.",
      "D": "Cost of discharging from the collecting vehicle."
    },
    "correct": "D",
    "reason": "Cost of discharging from the collecting vehicle is not an adjustment to the PAPP as it occurs after delivery."
  },
  "100": {
    "question": "Which of the following is not an Adjustment to the PAPP?",
    "choices": {
      "A": "Cost of design done in a third country.",
      "B": "Cost of design at the country of importation the design of which is supplied to the foreign supplier.",
      "C": "Selling commission.",
      "D": "Cost of raw materials produced at the country of importation and supplied to the foreign supplier."
    },
    "correct": "B",
    "reason": "Cost of design at the country of importation is not an adjustment to the PAPP; it is an assist but not an adjustment."
  },
  "101": {
    "question": "In determining the dutiable value using Method Five the information needed are supplied by the foreign supplier. What are the two (2) important considerations that must be considered if the District Collector would want to verify the supplied information at the country of exportation?",
    "choices": {
      "A": "Importer agrees to the verification and advance notice to the government of the country of exportation and no objection is raised by that government.",
      "B": "Importer agrees to the verification and the verification must be done at the country of exportation by the Philippine Consul General assigned to that country.",
      "C": "The Philippine Foreign Affairs Secretary must issue a note verbale to the Ambassador assigned to the Philippines by the country of exportation.",
      "D": "The District Collector cannot make any verification because custom law may only be enforced within the Philippine territory."
    },
    "correct": "A",
    "reason": "Verification in the exporting country requires importer agreement and advance notice to the exporting government with no objection raised."
  },
  "102": {
    "question": "In 'D' terms transaction which of the following charges is considered as adjustment to the price actually paid or payable?",
    "choices": {
      "A": "Marine cargo insurance from port of exportation to port of entry.",
      "B": "Export clearance expenses at the country of exportation.",
      "C": "Freight from port of exportation to port of entry.",
      "D": "None of the choices."
    },
    "correct": "D",
    "reason": "In D terms, the seller bears all costs; therefore, none of these charges are adjustments to the PAPP as they are already included in the seller's price."
  },
  "103": {
    "question": "Seller 'A' sent an offer sheet to Buyer 'B' for the supply of 'C' branded cosmetic products with the condition that the goods may only be sold in the Philippines through multi-level marketing (MLM). Is this an acceptable restriction for purposes of valuing the goods for customs purposes with the use of Method One?",
    "choices": {
      "A": "No, because it restricts the disposition of the goods.",
      "B": "Yes, because it is an acceptable restriction as it does not affect the value of the goods.",
      "C": "No, because the condition is such that the 'A' has control over the goods even if already delivered to 'B'.",
      "D": "Any of the choices, if there is no portion of the subsequent proceeds in the resale of the goods that will accrue to the benefit of 'A'."
    },
    "correct": "B",
    "reason": "A restriction that limits the method of resale but does not substantially affect the value of the goods is acceptable under Method One."
  },
  "104": {
    "question": "What shall generally be considered for the use of Method Five in determining customs value?",
    "choices": {
      "A": "That there is relationship between buyer and seller.",
      "B": "That the Philippines has diplomatic relationship with the government of the seller.",
      "C": "That the Department of Foreign Affairs (DFA) will be involved if there would be issues with the foreign seller.",
      "D": "All of the choices."
    },
    "correct": "A",
    "reason": "Method Five (Computed Value) is generally used when there is a relationship between buyer and seller, or when other methods are not applicable."
  },
  "105": {
    "question": "For purposes of using Method Four to determine the customs value of an importation of importer 'A' which is still in customs custody may a previous importation of 'A' of the same goods being sold at the customs territory be used?",
    "choices": {
      "A": "No, as this would constitute conflict of interest.",
      "B": "No, as this is not in the rules of the WTO Valuation Agreement (WVA).",
      "C": "Yes, provided that the buyer in the customs territory is not related to 'A'.",
      "D": "It depends on the nature of the goods as per determination by the Commissioner of Customs."
    },
    "correct": "C",
    "reason": "A previous importation of the same goods by the same importer may be used for Method Four, provided the buyer in the customs territory is not related to the seller."
  },
  "106": {
    "question": "JOHN RUIZZEL, Inc. imported 3,000 units of Ceramic Flower Vase at CIF price of $15.00 per unit from seller ELAYCA Trading in China. After subsequent resale, JOHN RUIZZEL, Inc. will remit to ELAYCA Trading the equivalent to 5% of the agreed CIF price. Furthermore, JOHN RUIZZEL, Inc. will pay commission to his agent that arranged the sale between the buyer and seller in the amount of $5,000.00. However, JOHN RUIZZEL, Inc. decided to supply the moulds amounting to 3,000.00 needed by ELAYCA Trading for the production of the said Ceramic Flower Vase but since JOHN RUIZZEL, Inc. insisted as that it was their importation, it is provided free of charge. Compute for the total Transaction Value under method 1 if the exchange rate is P50.00/US1.00.",
    "choices": {
      "A": "P 2,762,500.00",
      "B": "P 2,512,500.00",
      "C": "P 2,362,500.00",
      "D": "P 2,250,000.00"
    },
    "correct": "B",
    "reason": "CIF = 3,000 x $15.00 = $45,000. Addition of 5% of CIF remitted to the seller after resale = $2,250. Moulds supplied free of charge (assist) = $3,000. The $5,000 paid to JOHN RUIZZEL's own agent for arranging/sourcing the purchase is a buying commission, which is excluded from the transaction value. Total = $45,000 + $2,250 + $3,000 = $50,250 x P50.00 = P2,512,500.00."
  },
  "107": {
    "question": "A shipment of rice consigned to NFA arrived at Port of Cebu with total FOB value of $ 15,000.00. The freight charges per Bill Lading shows $1,200.00. Compute for the dutiable freight?",

      "B": "$ 1,200.00",
      "C": "$ 1,300.00",

  "108": {

  "109": {

      "C": "$ 1,260.00",

  "110": {

  "113": {

  "115": {
    "question": "A shipment of 1x20' STC: Ethyl Alcohol arrived at Port of Batangas with total CFR value of 35,000.00. The invoice shows freight charges of 2,500.00. Importer procured local insurance premium worth P 50,000.00 with certification and O.R. presented to BOC. The freight charge per bill of lading is $ 2,400.00. Compute for the dutiable freight if the exchange rate is P50.00/$1.00?",
    "choices": {
      "A": "$ 2,500.00",
      "B": "$ 1,250.00",
      "C": "$ 2,400.00",
      "D": "$ 1,300.00"
    },
    "correct": "A",
    "reason": "Dutiable freight is the higher of the freight shown in the commercial invoice ($2,500.00) or the Bill of Lading ($2,400.00), per CMO 22-2007. Since the invoice amount is higher, it is used: $2,500.00."
  },
  "116": {
    "question": "A major supermarket situated at the Mall of Asia, Pasay City, Manila imported 15,000 cans of Celsius energy drinks containing sucralose as a non-caloric artificial sweetener. Which is the total specific tax, net of value added tax, if each can have volume capacity of 50 centiliters? Note: Adopted from CuBLE 2021.",
    "choices": {
      "A": "P 90,000.00",
      "B": "P 45,000.00",
      "C": "P 450,000.00",
      "D": "P 42,000.00"
    },
    "correct": "B",
    "reason": "Sucralose is a non-caloric sweetener, not high fructose corn syrup, so the P6.00/liter rate applies (not the P12/liter HFCS rate). 15,000 cans x 0.5L x P6.00 = P45,000.00, net of VAT."
  },
  "117": {
    "question": "Arriving at the Ninoy Aquino International Airport was a shipment of 300 cases powdered juice drinks containing saccharide mixture of high fructose sweetener derived from corn. Each case contains 200 tetra packs with each pack weighing 75 grams. Based on the serving instruction of dissolving each pack with 100 centiliters of water, which is the total specific tax, VAT included? Note: Adopted from CuBLE 2021.",
    "choices": {
      "A": "P 360,000.00",
      "B": "P 820,000.00",
      "C": "P 806,400.00",
      "D": "P 403,200.00"
    },
    "correct": "C",
    "reason": "Total packs = 300 x 200 = 60,000. 100cl = 1L. Tax = P12/L (sweetened beverages under TRAIN). Base tax = 60,000 x 1 x P12 = P720,000. With VAT = P806,400."
  },
  "118": {
    "question": "A leading convenience store imported 300 cases Full Energy Drink with Non-Caloric Sweetener of 24 cans with 50 cl per case; 450 boxes having 10 packs per box of Energen cereal beverage using pure caloric sweeteners with 2.5 dl per pack; and 300 boxes with 12 packs per box of OldTown White 3-in-1 Coffee mix of 180 ml using purely caloric sweeteners. Compute for the total excise tax of Energen Cereal Beverage, exclusive of value added tax.",
    "choices": {
      "A": "P 7,560.00",
      "B": "P 6,750.00",
      "C": "P 13,500.00",
      "D": "P 15,120.00"
    },
    "correct": "B",
    "reason": "Energen: 450 boxes x 10 packs = 4,500 packs. 2.5dl = 0.25L. Tax = P6.00/L (caloric sweetener rate). Total = 4,500 x 0.25 x P6.00 = P6,750.00, exclusive of VAT."
  },
  "119": {
    "question": "A leading convenience store imported 300 cases Full Energy Drink with Non-Caloric Sweetener of 24 cans with 50 cl per case; 450 boxes having 10 packs per box of Energen cereal beverage using pure caloric sweeteners with 2.5 dl per pack; and 300 boxes with 12 packs per box of OldTown White 3-in-1 Coffee mix of 180 ml using purely caloric sweeteners. Compute for the total excise tax of OldTown White 3-in-1 Coffee, net of VAT.",

    },

    "reason": "OldTown White 3-in-1 Coffee mix contains caloric sweeteners but is classified as coffee mix, which is exempt from sweetened beverage tax under TRAIN Law."

  "120": {
    "question": "REDHAIR Dealership, Inc. imported 1 unit of 2026-year model Ford Mustang Ecoboost powered by Internal Combustion Engine in a 1x20' with Gross Importer's Selling Price P3,862,500.00, inclusive of ET and VAT amounted to P637,500.00 while the dealer's SRP, net of ET and VAT, is P4,012,500.00. The importation by REDHAIR Dealership, Inc. has a total customs value and miscellaneous expenses of $34,500.00 and P15,750.00, respectively. The freight indicated in the bill of lading is $1,500.00 per container. Using exchange rate of P55.00/$1.00, compute for the total AVT.",
    "choices": {
      "A": "P 645,000.00",
      "B": "P 675,000.00",
      "C": "P 665,000.00",
      "D": "P 655,000.00"
    },
    "correct": "A",
    "reason": "Net ISP = Gross ISP - ET - VAT = P3,862,500 - P637,500 = P3,225,000. AVT = 20% = P645,000."
  },
  "121": {
    "question": "SABO Corporation, a car dealer in Mandaluyong imported 15 units of hybrid automobiles, 2026-year model, 7-seater, 2,000cc engine displacement. All units are of the same variant and each unit had a gross manufacturer's selling price of P1,950,000.00 inclusive of the excise tax & VAT. The dealer's suggested retail price, net of VAT and ET, amounted to P1,900,700.00 per unit while the ad valorem & value added taxes had an aggregate sum of P250,000.00 per unit. The total cost and importation had a total value of 1,728,000.00. Compute for the total taxable base to be used in determining Ad Valorem Tax.",
    "choices": {
      "A": "P 1,520,560.00",
      "B": "P 1,700,000.00",
      "C": "P 1,728,000.00",
      "D": "P 1,920,000.00"
    },
    "correct": "B",
    "reason": "Since SABO Corporation is a dealer importing the vehicles FOR SALE, the Ad Valorem Tax base is the net manufacturer's/importer's selling price, not the cost of importation (the cost-of-importation/landed-value basis applies only to imported automobiles NOT for sale). Net MSP = Gross MSP - (AVT + VAT) = P1,950,000.00 - P250,000.00 = P1,700,000.00."
  },
  "122": {
    "question": "Facts Given: Total Dutiable Value: P750,000.00, Total Misc. Exp: P12,500.00. The rate of duty is 10%. As a Customs Broker, compute for the total Landed Cost.",
    "choices": {
      "A": "P 837,500.00",
      "B": "P 762,500.00",
      "C": "P 726,050.00",
      "D": "P 835,700.00"
    },
    "correct": "A",
    "reason": "Duty = 10% x P750,000 = P75,000. Landed Cost = DV + Duty + Misc = P750,000 + P75,000 + P12,500 = P837,500."
  },
  "123": {
    "question": "Importation of assorted Christmas decors arrived at the MICP with a dutiable value of $32,500.00. The Bureau of Customs has ascertained that the requirements under CMO No. 22-2007 has been complied with. The arrastre charges, wharfage dues, Customs Documentary Stamps, Customs Brokerage fee and Import Processing Charge amounted to P15,250.00 and rate of duty is 10% ad valorem. Prevailing rate of exchange is P 54.50/$1.00. As a Customs Broker, compute for the total VAT.",
    "choices": {
      "A": "P 2,199,260.00",
      "B": "P 235,635.00",
      "C": "P 2,150,260.00",
      "D": "P 250,600.00"
    },
    "correct": "B",
    "reason": "VAT = 12% x (DV + Duty + Misc) = 12% x P1,963,625 = P235,635."
  },
  "124": {
    "question": "The National Food Authority imported 5,000 bags of wheat flour with a total FOB Value $50,000.00. The bill of lading shows total freight charges of $5,000.00. The shipment is covered by GSIS insurance in the amount of P 45,750.00. The total miscellaneous expenses amounted to P 15,500.00. The ad valorem duty is 1%. Use the exchange rate P45.75/$1.00. Compute for the dutiable value.",
    "choices": {
      "A": "P 2,562,000.00",
      "B": "P 2,630,625.00",
      "C": "P 2,584,875.00",
      "D": "P 2,550,000.00"
    },
    "correct": "A",
    "reason": "FOB = $50,000 x P45.75 = P2,287,500. Freight = $5,000 x P45.75 = P228,750. Insurance = P45,750. DV = P2,287,500 + P228,750 + P45,750 = P2,562,000."
  },
  "125": {
    "question": "The National Food Authority imported 5,000 bags of wheat flour with a total FOB Value $50,000.00. The bill of lading shows total freight charges of $5,000.00. The shipment is covered by GSIS insurance in the amount of P 45,750.00. The total miscellaneous expenses amounted to P 15,500.00. The ad valorem duty is 1%. Use the exchange rate P45.75/$1.00.     "choices": {

      "B": "$ 11,333.00",
      "C": "$ 11,433.00",

  "366": {
    "question": "Except for one, the following are not regarded as wholly obtained goods under Article 27 of the ATIGA ROO:",
    "choices": {
      "A": "Processed mixed fruits derived from plants grown and harvested in the Philippines and packed with imported transparent plastic bags for retail sale in Singapore.",
      "B": "Canned sardines processed in the high seas on board factory ships manned entirely by Filipino crew. The ship is Japanese owned with its flag on it.",
      "C": "A Thai-speaking parrot trapped in Malaysia, taught how to speak Malay, then exported to Brunei.",
      "D": "The Philippines exports steel ingots derived from melting steel scrap gathered from the stamping plant of a Filipino-owned appliance manufacturer in Indonesia."
    },
    "correct": "A",
    "reason": "Under ATIGA Article 26/27, plants grown and harvested in the exporting Member State are wholly obtained; imported retail packaging does not affect this status. By contrast: (B) fails because the vessel is Japanese-flagged/owned, not registered to fly the Philippine flag; (C) fails because the parrot was trapped in Malaysia, not in Brunei (the claimed exporting State); (D) fails because the scrap was sourced from a plant located in Indonesia, not the Philippines - foreign ownership of that plant does not cure the foreign sourcing."
  },
  "367": {
    "question": "Which of the following groups of different criteria defines the concept of sufficient working or processing under the substantial transformation provision of the ATIGA ROO?",
    "choices": {
      "A": "Change in Tariff Classification criterion, Value-added criterion, and Technical Requirement criterion",
      "B": "Change in Tariff Classification criterion, Wholly-obtained criterion, and Value-added criterion",
      "C": "Value-added criterion, Wholly-obtained criterion, and Technical Requirement criterion",
      "D": "Value-added criterion, Substantial Transformation criterion, and Change in Tariff Classification criterion"
    },
    "correct": "A",
    "reason": "Sufficient working or processing is defined by Change in Tariff Classification, Value-added, and Technical Requirement criteria."
  },
  "368": {
    "question": "Under the Build-Down Method formula for the calculation of the RVC value of the final good destined for export under the AANZFTA ROO, what element is subtracted from the FOB value?",
    "choices": {
      "A": "CIF Value of Non-Originating Materials",
      "B": "FOB Value of Non-Originating Materials",
      "C": "CIF Value of Originating Materials",
      "D": "AANZFTA Material Costs"
    },
    "correct": "A",
    "reason": "Under the AANZFTA Build-Down Method, RVC = (FOB - VNM)/FOB x 100, where VNM (Value of Non-Originating Materials) is measured at its CIF value at the time of importation - not its FOB value."
  },
  "369": {
    "question": "Under the De Minimis provision of AANZFTA, which of the following statements is true?",
    "choices": {
      "A": "The value of all non-originating materials used in the production of the good that did not undergo the required change in tariff classification does not exceed 10% of the FOB Value.",
      "B": "For a good provided under Chapters 50 to 63 of the HS Code, the weight of all non-originating materials that did not undergo the required change in tariff classification does not exceed 10% of the total weight of the good.",
      "C": "The value of the materials that did not satisfy the change in tariff classification shall be included in the value of non-originating materials for any applicable regional value content requirement.",
      "D": "All the statements are true."
    },
    "correct": "D",
    "reason": "All the statements are true under the De Minimis provision of AANZFTA."
  },
  "370": {
    "question": "What is the required range of the Regional Value Content to be eligible for partial accumulation under the ATIGA ROO?",
    "choices": {
      "A": "From 30% to 40%",
      "B": "From 40% to not more than 60%",
      "C": "Less than 40%",
      "D": "From 20% to less than 40%"
    },
    "correct": "D",
    "reason": "Under the ATIGA ROO, partial accumulation applies when the material/good achieves a Regional Value Content of at least 20% but less than 40%. A good with RVC of 40% or more would qualify for full accumulation (treated as fully originating)."
  },
  "371": {
    "question": "Which one among the following is a set of principles used to determine the country of origin of a good for purposes of international trade?",

      "A": "Tariff Classification Ruling",
      "B": "Certificate of Origin",
      "C": "General Interpretative Rules",
      "D": "Rules of Origin"
    },
    "correct": "D",
    "reason": "Rules of Origin are the principles used to determine the country of origin of a good."
  },
  "372": {
    "question": "What is the specific term referred to goods that are made entirely in the exporting country exclusively from originating materials produced in that same country?",
    "choices": {
      "A": "Substantially transformed goods",
      "B": "Originating goods",
      "C": "Wholly-Obtained goods",
      "D": "Exportable goods"
    },
    "correct": "C",
    "reason": "Wholly-Obtained goods are made entirely in the exporting country from originating materials."
  },
  "373": {
    "question": "The Product Specific Rule (PSR) of this FTA requires an RVC 35% plus a Change in Tariff Subheading. What FTA is being referred to?",
    "choices": {
      "A": "AKFTA",
      "B": "AIFTA",
      "C": "ATIGA",
      "D": "ACFTA"
    },
    "correct": "A",
    "reason": "AKFTA (ASEAN-Korea FTA) requires RVC 35% plus Change in Tariff Subheading (CTSH) as Product Specific Rule."
  },
  "374": {
    "question": "Which among the following non-originating parts does not confer a CTH under the AKFTA ROO for wall fans classified under HS code 8414.512?",
    "choices": {
      "A": "Motor (HS 8501.10)",
      "B": "Cover (HS 8414.90)",
      "C": "Electrical cord (HS 8544.42)",
      "D": "Switches (HS 8536.50)"
    },
    "correct": "B",
    "reason": "Cover (HS 8414.90) is classified under the same heading 8414 as the final product, so it does not confer a Change in Tariff Heading (CTH)."
  },
  "375": {
    "question": "Under the ATIGA ROO, what is the General Rule in determining whether a not wholly produced or obtained product for export to another ASEAN Member State is originating or not?",
    "choices": {
      "A": "Minimum threshold of RVC 40%",
      "B": "ASEAN content of not less than 40% or CTC",
      "C": "ASEAN content of not less than 40% or CTH",
      "D": "ASEAN content of not less than 40% or CTSH"
    },
    "correct": "C",
    "reason": "The ATIGA General Rule for goods not wholly obtained is: ASEAN/Regional Value Content of not less than 40%, OR a Change in Tariff Heading (CTH) at the 4-digit level - not the broader, undefined 'CTC' label."
  },
  "376": {
    "question": "Which among the following choices is the correct tariff rate applied for a product imported into the Philippines and covered by an e-Form D issued in Viet Nam with the box 'For Partial Cumulation' checked?",
    "choices": {
      "A": "MFN rate of duty",
      "B": "ATIGA rate of duty",
      "C": "Duty and excise tax free importation",
      "D": "Partial of the ATIGA rate of duty"
    },
    "correct": "D",
    "reason": "Partial cumulation applies a partial ATIGA rate of duty."
  },
  "377": {
    "question": "Digital color printers classified under HS 8443.32 were manufactured in Indonesia and exported to the Philippines. The non-originating parts were electric motors (HS 8501.20) from USA and electric cables (HS 8544.20) from China. If the ROO used in the manufacture of subject printers was CTH, were the goods considered originating or non-originating pursuant to the CTC rule of the ATIGA ROO?",
    "choices": {
      "A": "Not originating since the classification of both the non-originating parts are different from the classification of the final product.",
      "B": "It is originating because the exported good came from Indonesia.",
      "C": "Not originating since USA and China are not Party to the AFTA.",
      "D": "It is originating since there was a tariff shift."
    },
    "correct": "D",
    "reason": "Since the non-originating parts (HS 8501, 8544) are classified under different headings from the final product (8443), a Change in Tariff Heading (CTH) has occurred, making the product originating."
  },
  "378": {
    "question": "Which of the following choices is considered as Neutral Elements under the ATIGA ROO?",
    "choices": {
      "A": "Spare parts, tools and instructional materials exported with the good.",
      "B": "Packaging and packing materials exported with the good for retail sale.",
      "C": "Spare parts, materials, supplies used in the maintenance of equipment and buildings.",
      "D": "Slaughtering of animals by chopping into parts."
    },
    "correct": "C",
    "reason": "Spare parts, materials, and supplies used in maintenance of equipment and buildings are considered Neutral Elements."
  },
  "379": {
    "question": "In the numerator of the Build-Down Formula used in the calculation of the Regional Value Content under the AKFTA, what element is deducted from the FOB value of the final product destined for export?",
    "choices": {
      "A": "Profit, overhead costs, material costs and other local costs",
      "B": "CIF Value of non-originating materials",
      "C": "FOB Value of originating materials",
      "D": "FOB Value of non-originating materials"
    },
    "correct": "B",
    "reason": "Under the AKFTA Build-Down Formula, the value deducted from the FOB value of the final good is the CIF value of the non-originating materials, not their FOB value."
  },
  "380": {
    "question": "Under the AKFTA ROO, what are defined as the rules which specify that the materials have undergone a change in tariff classification or a specific manufacturing or processing operation or satisfy a regional value content or a combination of any of these criteria?",
    "choices": {
      "A": "Product Specific Rules",
      "B": "RVC or CTC Rules",
      "C": "Mixed Rules",
      "D": "Substantial Transformation Criterion"
    },
    "correct": "A",
    "reason": "Product Specific Rules (PSR) specify the criteria for materials to be considered originating."
  },
  "381": {
    "question": "Which ASEAN + FTA includes 'Goods taken from outer space provided that they are obtained by the Party or a person of that Party' in its definition for wholly obtained goods?",
    "choices": {
      "A": "ASEAN-China Free Trade Area (ACFTA)",
      "B": "ASEAN-Japan Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (AJCEPA)",
      "C": "ASEAN-Korea Free Trade Area (AKFTA)",
      "D": "ASEAN-Australia-New Zealand Free Trade Area (AANZFTA)"
    },
    "correct": "B",
    "reason": "AJCEPA includes 'goods taken from outer space' in its definition of wholly obtained goods."
  },
  "382": {
    "question": "Which of the following statements is erroneous under the provisions of Article 32 (Non-Qualifying Operations) of the JPEPA ROO?",
    "choices": {
      "A": "Operations to ensure the preservation of products in good condition during transport and storage.",
      "B": "The goods shall be considered to satisfy the requirement of change in tariff classification or specific manufacturing or processing operation.",
      "C": "Changes of packaging, breaking up and assembly of packages.",
      "D": "Disassembly."
    },
    "correct": "B",
    "reason": "Article 32 states that non-qualifying operations do not confer origin; the goods shall not be considered to satisfy the change in tariff classification."
  },
  "383": {
    "question": "Under the ACFTA Agreement, what Certificate of Origin should be issued in China for exports of goods to the Philippines wherein the raw materials used in its production were Indonesia-originating and constituted about 60% of the FOB value of the export good?",
    "choices": {
      "A": "CO Form C",
      "B": "Pro-forma Invoice",
      "C": "CO Form D",
      "D": "CO Form E"
    },
    "correct": "D",
    "reason": "CO Form E is used under ACFTA for exports from China to ASEAN countries."
  },
  "384": {
    "question": "Which one among the following choices is a type of invoice issued in Hong Kong for a product originating in Viet Nam for export to the Philippines under the ATIGA?",
    "choices": {
      "A": "Recurring Invoice",
      "B": "Back-to-back Certificate of Origin (Form D)",
      "C": "Third-Party Invoice",
      "D": "Commercial Invoice"
    },
    "correct": "C",
    "reason": "When goods are transshipped through a third country, a Third-Party Invoice is issued."
  },
  "385": {
    "question": "Which among the following choices is a type of Proof of Origin issued by the BOC for various types of sports shoes destined for Indonesia based on the presented original Certificate of Origin issued in Viet Nam for the same goods transshipped through the Philippines?",
    "choices": {
      "A": "Non-Preferential Certificate of Origin",
      "B": "Back-to-back Certificate of Origin (Form D)",
      "C": "Electronic Certificate of Origin (e-Form D)",
      "D": "Origin Declaration"
    },
    "correct": "B",
    "reason": "A Back-to-back Certificate of Origin (Form D) is issued when goods are transshipped through an intermediate party."
  },
  "386": {
    "question": "Which of the following statements is correct per Rule 7 of the ATIGA OCP?",
    "choices": {
      "A": "The exporter retains the original copy of the duly signed CO Form D.",
      "B": "The issuing authority retains the original copy of the duly issued Certificate of Origin Form D.",
      "C": "The importer retains the original copy of the duly issued Certificate of Origin Form D.",
      "D": "The Customs Authority of the importing Member State retains the original copy of the duly issued Certificate of Origin Form D."
    },
    "correct": "C",
    "reason": "The importer retains the original copy of the CO Form D to claim preferential tariff treatment."
  },
  "387": {
    "question": "To be eligible in availing the concession rates under the ATIGA, the product imported into the Philippines must meet the following, except for one. Which one among the following choices is not a requirement?",
    "choices": {
      "A": "The product should satisfy the ASEAN content of at least 40% value-added.",
      "B": "The product should be accompanied by a Certificate of Origin Form D.",
      "C": "The product should be in the CEPT Schedule Inclusion List of both the importing and exporting countries and that tariffs on the product of both parties fall within the same tariff band, i.e., above 20% or 20% and below.",
      "D": "The importer should have secured a CO from the BOC."
    },
    "correct": "D",
    "reason": "The CO is issued by the exporting country's issuing authority, not by the importer from the BOC."
  },
  "388": {
    "question": "Which of the following choices is true when it comes to the issuances of Certificates of Origin for wholly-obtained goods?",
    "choices": {
      "A": "The Philippines issued Certificate of Origin Form D for export to Indonesia under the AFTA.",
      "B": "Lao PDR issued Certificate of Origin Form E for export to Indonesia under the ACFTA.",
      "C": "Singapore issued Certificate of Origin Form AANZ for export to Indonesia under the AANZFTA.",
      "D": "All the statements are true."
    },
    "correct": "A",
    "reason": "The Philippines issued CO Form D for export to Indonesia under AFTA/ATIGA; the other statements contain incorrect CO forms for their respective FTAs."
  },
  "389": {
    "question": "A consignment of 5 units of 2-burner gas stoves originating in the Philippines valued at US185.00 is destined for export to Lao PDR under the provisions of the ATIGA. Which one among the choices below is applicable to said transaction?",
    "choices": {
      "A": "The production of CO Form D shall be waived and the use of a simplified declaration by the exporter that the gas stoves have originated in the Philippines will be accepted.",
      "B": "The exporter shall apply in writing to the Bureau of Customs to issue the required CO Form D in order for the goods to be eligible for the preferential ATIGA rate in Lao PDR.",
      "C": "With the value of only at US185.00, the gas stoves although Philippine originating will not be eligible for the tariff concessions of the ATIGA.",
      "D": "The said gas stoves will automatically be charged with the MFN rate in Lao PDR."
    },
    "correct": "A",
    "reason": "Under ATIGA, shipments with FOB value of US200.00 and below are waived from the requirement of CO Form D and may use a simplified declaration."
  },
  "390": {
    "question": "Under the ATIGA and ASEAN plus FTAs, which of the following groups of countries had Customs designated to issue Certificates of Origin?",
    "choices": {
      "A": "China, Philippines and South Korea",
      "B": "South Korea, Philippines and Thailand",
      "C": "China, Philippines and Singapore",

    },
    "correct": "A",
    "reason": "China, Philippines, and South Korea have Customs designated to issue Certificates of Origin."
  },
  "391": {
    "question": "What is the composition of the Certificate of Origin Form D?",
    "choices": {
      "A": "2 originals, 2 carbon copies",
      "B": "1 original, 1 duplicate carbon copy, and 1 triplicate carbon copy",
      "C": "1 original, 2 duplicate carbon copies, 1 triplicate carbon copy",
      "D": "1 original and 3 duplicate carbon copies"
    },
    "correct": "B",
    "reason": "CO Form D consists of 1 original, 1 duplicate, and 1 triplicate carbon copy."
  },
  "392": {
    "question": "What is the formal paper size of a Certificate of Origin Form D under the ATIGA?",
    "choices": {
      "A": "Letter size",
      "B": "ISO US Folio size",
      "C": "Legal size",
      "D": "ISO A4 size"
    },
    "correct": "D",
    "reason": "The Certificate of Origin Form D under ATIGA uses ISO A4 paper size."
  },
  "393": {
    "question": "South Korea imported steel bars (HS 7214.91) from Japan where it was cut to size, welded, painted and assembled into door frames (HS 7308.30). If the agreed PSR is change to this Subheading from any other Heading, what Certificate of Origin should be issued to avail of the concession rate here in the Philippines?",
    "choices": {
      "A": "CO Form JP",
      "B": "CO Form AK",
      "C": "CO Form RCEP",
      "D": "CO Form AJ"
    },
    "correct": "B",
    "reason": "CO Form AK is used under AKFTA for trade between ASEAN and South Korea."
  },
  "394": {
    "question": "A Philippine originating product covered by a Certificate of Origin Form 'D' is valid and eligible for preferential import tariff when exported to which of the following choices?",
    "choices": {
      "A": "Indonesia",
      "B": "Malaysia",
      "C": "Brunei",
      "D": "Any of the above"
    },
    "correct": "D",
    "reason": "CO Form D is used under ATIGA, which covers all ASEAN Member States including Indonesia, Malaysia, and Brunei."
  },
  "395": {
    "question": "What is the Certificate of Origin used under the AHKFTA Agreement?",
    "choices": {
      "A": "CO Form A",
      "B": "CO Form AK",
      "C": "CO Form AHK",
      "D": "CO Form D"
    },
    "correct": "C",
    "reason": "CO Form AHK is used under the ASEAN-Hong Kong Free Trade Agreement (AHKFTA)."
  },
  "396": {
    "question": "Which one among the following are a set of principles used to determine the country of origin of a good for purposes of international trade?",
    "choices": {
      "A": "Tariff Classification Ruling",
      "B": "Certificate of Origin",
      "C": "General Interpretative Rules",
      "D": "Rules of Origin"
    },
    "correct": "D",
    "reason": "Rules of Origin are the principles used to determine the country of origin of a good."
  },
  "397": {
    "question": "Under the ROO, what provision is put in place to ensure that no further processing takes place in a third country or non-Party, wherein goods leaving the jurisdiction of a Party are identical to those imported into another Party?",
    "choices": {
      "A": "Direct consignment",
      "B": "Transshipment",
      "C": "Third-Party Shipment",
      "D": "Straight Shipment"
    },
    "correct": "A",
    "reason": "Direct consignment ensures goods are not processed in a third country and remain identical from export to import."
  },
  "398": {
    "question": "Which one among the following choices is the correct requirement of the De Minimis Rule under the ATIGA ROO for a non-originating material that did not meet the CTC?",
    "choices": {
      "A": "To have a value that exceeds 15% of the FOB value of the final exported good.",
      "B": "To have an RVC at a minimum of 40% of the FOB value of the exported good.",
      "C": "To have a classification that is different from the exported product.",
      "D": "To have a value that does not exceed 10% of the FOB value of the exported good."
    },
    "correct": "D",
    "reason": "The De Minimis Rule allows non-originating materials that did not meet the CTC up to 10% of the FOB value."
  },
  "399": {
    "question": "Under the ROO, what is the specific term referred to goods that are made entirely in the exporting country from materials produced in that same country?",
    "choices": {
      "A": "Originating goods",
      "B": "Conferred goods",
      "C": "Substantially Transformed goods",
      "D": "Wholly-Obtained goods"
    },
    "correct": "D",
    "reason": "Wholly-Obtained goods are made entirely in the exporting country from materials produced in that same country."
  },
  "400": {
    "question": "Under the ATIGA ROO, what other way could a non-originating material which failed the CTC tariff shift requirement qualify as originating?",
    "choices": {
      "A": "Regional Value Content Rule",
      "B": "Substantial Transformation Rule",
      "C": "De Minimis Rule",
      "D": "Specific Process Rule"
    },
    "correct": "C",
    "reason": "A non-originating material that fails the required tariff shift (CTC) can still be tolerated under the ATIGA De Minimis Rule, provided its value does not exceed 10% of the FOB value of the final good - this is distinct from choosing the RVC method as an alternative origin criterion for the good as a whole."
  },
  "401": {
    "question": "What origin criterion of the ATIGA ROO requires the final product to be classified under an HS code that is different from the HS code classification of non-originating materials, parts or components used in its production?",
    "choices": {
      "A": "Product Specific Rules",
      "B": "Substantial Transformation",
      "C": "Regional Value Content",
      "D": "Change in Tariff Classification"
    },
    "correct": "D",
    "reason": "Change in Tariff Classification (CTC) requires the final product to be classified under a different HS code from its non-originating materials."
  },
  "402": {
    "question": "Under the ROO substantial transformation, what is the term used in describing a change in classification in the HS nomenclature?",
    "choices": {
      "A": "Classification change",
      "B": "Code switch",
      "C": "Tariff shift",
      "D": "Tariff change"
    },
    "correct": "C",
    "reason": "A 'Tariff shift' is the term used to describe a change in classification under the HS nomenclature."
  },
  "403": {
    "question": "Under the ROO, the Direct Method used in the determination of Regional Value Content is also known as which one among the following choices?",
    "choices": {
      "A": "One Rule Method",
      "B": "Build-Up Method",
      "C": "Full Method",
      "D": "Straight-Forward Method"
    },
    "correct": "B",
    "reason": "The Direct Method for RVC calculation is also known as the Build-Up Method."
  },
  "404": {
    "question": "A product coming from an ASEAN Member State cannot be granted the ATIGA rate of duty by the importing ASEAN Member State if:",
    "choices": {
      "A": "the importation is with a duly issued e-Form D",
      "B": "the product is wholly-obtained in one ASEAN Member State",
      "C": "the value of originating materials used in the manufacture of the product is not less than 40% of the FOB value of the product",
      "D": "the value of non-originating materials used in the manufacture of the product exceeds 60% of the FOB value of the product"
    },
    "correct": "D",
    "reason": "If non-originating materials exceed 60% of FOB value, the product does not meet the 40% ASEAN content requirement and cannot receive ATIGA rates."
  },
  "405": {
    "question": "Which one among the following choices is a type of ROO used to implement trade remedy measures namely anti-dumping, safeguards, and subsidy?",
    "choices": {
      "A": "Product Specific ROO",
      "B": "Non-Preferential ROO",
      "C": "CTC ROO",

    "correct": "B",
    "reason": "Non-Preferential Rules of Origin are used to implement trade remedy measures like anti-dumping, safeguards, and subsidies."
  },
  "406": {
    "question": "Where would an exporter file for a Ruling on Rules of Origin pursuant to CMTA Sec. 1102, to cover their locally produced product destined to a Preferential Trade Agreement Partner?",

  "407": {
    "question": "Under the ACFTA Agreement, what Certificate of Origin should be issued in China for exports of goods to the Philippines wherein the raw materials used in its production were Indonesia originating and constituted about 60% of the FOB value of the export good?",
    "choices": {

  "408": {
    "question": "A Certified Exporter is authorized to issue this type of Proof of Origin under the ATIGA. Which one is being referred to?",

  "409": {

  },
  "410": {

  "411": {

  "412": {

  "413": {

  "414": {

  "415": {

    "choices": {

  "416": {

  "417": {
    "question": "What type of Proof of Origin must be secured for an exported product to be eligible for the preferential tariff rate of the importing country under the Agreement between the Philippines and Japan for an Economic Partnership?",

  },
  "418": {
    "question": "Which among the following is a document used in international trade, accomplished by the exporter or its agent and certified by an issuing body, used to formally attest that the products exported are wholly obtained, produced or manufactured in a particular Country?",
    "choices": {
      "A": "Commercial Invoice",
      "B": "Proof of Origin",
      "C": "Exporter Origin Certification",
      "D": "Manufacturer Statement of Origin Declaration"
    },
    "correct": "B",

  },
  "419": {
    "question": "Which one among the following refers to the procedures governing the issuance and verification of the Proof of Origin and the other related administrative matters for the purposes of implementing the rules of origin applicable to a preferential trade agreement?",
    "choices": {

      "B": "Certification Guidelines",
      "C": "Operational Certification Procedure",
      "D": "Issuance Procedures"
    },
    "correct": "C",
    "reason": "Operational Certification Procedure (OCP) governs the issuance and verification of Proof of Origin for a PTA."

  "420": {
    "question": "Under the OCP of the ROO, which of the following is referred to the designated body of a Party tasked to issue the Proof of Origin required to implement the ROO of each Preferential Trade Agreement?",
    "choices": {

      "B": "Trader Association",
      "C": "The Customs Authority",
      "D": "The Issuing Authority"
    },

  "429": {

  "430": {

  "432": {

  "433": {

  "434": {

  "435": {

  "438": {
    "question": "Under the ROO, the Indirect Method used in the determination of Regional Value Content is also known as which one among the following choices?",
