  },
  "439": {
    "question": "With reference to unfair trade practices caused by dumping pursuant to the provisions of Anti-Dumping Act of 1999, which one among the following choices refers to a transaction where the price is not affected by any relationship between the buyer and the seller, or if there is no compensation, reimbursement, benefit, or other consideration given in respect of the price?",
    "choices": {
      "A": "Non-compensatory Transaction",
      "B": "Arms-Length Transaction",
      "C": "Buyer and Seller Transaction",
      "D": "Beneficial Transaction"
    },
    "correct": "B",
    "reason": "An Arms-Length Transaction is one where the price is not affected by any relationship between buyer and seller."
  },
  "440": {
    "question": "It means the comparable price in the ordinary course of trade for the like product when meant for consumption in the exporting country or territory. Which among the following choices below this definition under R.A. No. 8752 being referred to?",
    "choices": {
      "A": "Ex-factory price at the point of sale for export",
      "B": "Export price to third country",
      "C": "Normal value",
      "D": "Seasonable market price"
    },
    "correct": "C",
    "reason": "Normal value is the comparable price in the ordinary course of trade for the like product in the exporting country."
  },
  "441": {
    "question": "This refers to the finding that the material injury suffered by the domestic industry is the direct result of the importation of the dumped imports. Which among the choices below being referred to under Anti-Dumping Act of 1999?",
    "choices": {
      "A": "Causality",
      "B": "Material Injury",
      "C": "Threat of Material Injury",
      "D": "Serious Injury"
    },
    "correct": "A",
    "reason": "Causality refers to the direct link between dumped imports and material injury to the domestic industry."
  },
  "442": {
    "question": "The following administrative reviews are mandated under Anti-Dumping Act of 1999, except for one. Which one is not?",
    "choices": {
      "A": "Sunset Review",
      "B": "Monitoring Review",
      "C": "Newcomer Review",
      "D": "Interim Review"
    },
    "correct": "B",
    "reason": "Monitoring Review is not mandated under the Anti-Dumping Act of 1999."
  },
  "443": {
    "question": "Pursuant to Countervailing Duty Act of 1999, the following are the modalities used in the determination of the price effects of dumped imports. Which one is not included?",
    "choices": {
      "A": "Price undercutting",
      "B": "Price suppression",
      "C": "Price depression",
      "D": "Price undertaking"
    },
    "correct": "D",

  },
  "444": {
    "question": "Under R.A. 8752, how many days the Secretary of Trade and Industry to make a preliminary determination of the need to impose provisional anti-dumping duty after receipt of the answers of the respondents including supporting documents?",
    "choices": {
      "A": "Not later than 20 working days",
      "B": "Not later than 20 calendar days",
      "C": "Not later than 30 calendar days",
      "D": "Not later than 30 working days"
    },
    "correct": "C",
    "reason": "Under R.A. 8752, the Secretary has not later than thirty (30) calendar days to make a preliminary determination."
  },
  "445": {
    "question": "The following choices below show the basis of determining an export price pursuant to R.A. No. 8752, except for one. Which one is not included?",
    "choices": {
      "A": "FOB price at the point of shipment",
      "B": "Ex-factory price at the point of sale for export",
      "C": "Importer's selling price to the first customers that are not related",
      "D": "Export price to third country"
    },
    "correct": "D",
    "reason": "Export price to third country is not a basis for determining export price under R.A. 8752."
  },
  "446": {
    "question": "Which government agency conducts the preliminary investigation to determine whether or not a provisional countervailing duty may be imposed on tomato pastes covered under Chapter 20?",
    "choices": {
      "A": "Department of Agriculture",
      "B": "Department of Trade and Industry-Bureau of Import Services",

      "D": "Bureau of Customs"

    "reason": "For agricultural products, the Department of Agriculture conducts the preliminary investigation for countervailing duties."
  },
  "447": {
    "question": "Which of the following choices refers to a determination that shall be based on facts and not merely on allegation, conjecture or remote possibility, and the change in circumstances which will create a situation in which the dumping will cause injury must be clearly foreseen and imminent?",
    "choices": {
      "A": "Determination of Material Injury",
      "B": "Determination of Serious Injury",
      "C": "Determination of Threat of Serious Injury",
      "D": "Determination of Threat of Material Injury"
    },
    "correct": "D",
    "reason": "Threat of Material Injury requires a determination based on facts, not conjecture, with clearly foreseen and imminent circumstances."
  },
  "448": {
    "question": "Which of the following refers to subsidies protected from countervailing action either because they are considered to be of particular value to have no or at most minimal trade-distorting effects?",
    "choices": {
      "A": "Non-Actionable Subsidies",
      "B": "Yellow Subsidies",
      "C": "Actionable Subsidies",
      "D": "Protected Subsidies"

    "reason": "Non-Actionable Subsidies are protected from countervailing action due to minimal trade-distorting effects."
  },
  "449": {
    "question": "Which of the following refers to any specific assistance (e.g., financial contribution, income or price support schemes) provided directly or indirectly by the US government in respect of the product exported to the Philippines, which benefits the US producer or exporter?",
    "choices": {
      "A": "Prohibited Subsidy",
      "B": "Actionable Subsidy",
      "C": "Non-actionable Subsidy",
      "D": "All of the choices"

    "correct": "B",
    "reason": "A subsidy that is specific and causes injury is an Actionable Subsidy."
  },
  "450": {
    "question": "What is the administrative review that is initiated when there is sufficient evidence that the expiry of the definitive anti-dumping duty would likely result in a continuation or recurrence of dumping and injury?",

      "B": "Administrative Review",
      "C": "Interim Review",
      "D": "Judicial Review"

  },
  "451": {
    "question": "A general safeguard measure shall not be applied to a product originating from a country whose share of total imports of the product is less than three percent (3%), provided, however, that countries with less than three percent (3%) share collectively account for not more than nine percent (9%) of the total imports. Which one of the following countries is being referred to?",
    "choices": {
      "A": "Developed country",
      "B": "Developing country",
      "C": "Underdeveloped country",
      "D": "Any of the ASEAN Member States"
    },
    "correct": "B",
    "reason": "The de minimis exception applies to developing countries with a share of less than 3% and collectively not more than 9%."
  },
  "452": {
    "question": "Pursuant to the provisions of R.A. No. 8800, which one among the following choices is not a form of definitive safeguard measure?",
    "choices": {
      "A": "A decrease in the tariff-rate quota (MAV) applied on the product",
      "B": "Imposition of quantitative restriction on imports",
      "C": "Tariff rate increase",
      "D": "Temporary prohibition of the product"
    },
    "correct": "D",
    "reason": "Temporary prohibition is not a form of definitive safeguard measure; it would be a provisional or emergency measure."
  },
  "453": {
    "question": "Pursuant to the provisions of R.A. No. 8752, which one among the following choices applied only after the DTI-BIS or DA has made preliminary affirmative determination no sooner than 60 days from the initiation of the case?",
    "choices": {
      "A": "Provisional measure",
      "B": "Dumping bond",
      "C": "Definitive duty",
      "D": "Temporary measure"

  },
  "454": {
    "question": "Which one among the following choices are types of subsidies that disciplines under the WTO Agreement on Subsidies and Countervailing cannot be subjected to either countervailing measures or other measures because they are applied across-the-board to all industries and not limited to specific industry or enterprise or group of enterprises or industries?",
    "choices": {
      "A": "Yellow subsidies",
      "B": "Green subsidies",
      "C": "Actionable subsidies",
      "D": "Red subsidies"
    },
    "correct": "B",
    "reason": "Green subsidies are non-specific subsidies applied across-the-board and are not subject to countervailing measures."
  },
  "455": {
    "question": "Under R.A. No. 8752, within (50) days from the receipt of the preliminary findings including records of the case from the Secretary, the Commission shall prepare and issue a Report which covers, among others, findings on product comparability, normal value, export price, volume of dumped imports, alleged injury to the domestic industry plus the evaluation of the results of the verification/ocular inspection conducted by the Commission.     "choices": {
      "A": "Preliminary Report",
      "B": "Final Report",

    },

    "reason": "The Final Report is issued within 50 days from receipt of preliminary findings."
  },
  "456": {
    "question": "What is the monetary requirement by the Secretary from the petitioner upon acceptance of a properly documented application, which will be utilized as bond to answer for any and all damages that the importer may sustain by reason of the filing of a frivolous petition under R.A. No. 8752?",
    "choices": {
      "A": "Monetary Bond",
      "B": "Provisional Bond",
      "C": "Assurance Bond",
      "D": "None of the choices"
    },

    "reason": "An Assurance Bond is required from the petitioner to cover damages from a frivolous petition."
  },
  "457": {
    "question": "What action plan which a domestic industry is required to submit, describes a set of quantified goals, specific plans, and timetables that a concerned industry commits to undertake in order to facilitate positive adjustment of the industry to import competition?",
    "choices": {
      "A": "Final Adjustment Plan",
      "B": "Specific and Quantifiable Plan",
      "C": "Final Positive Plan",
      "D": "Final Management Plan"
    },
    "correct": "A",

  },
  "458": {
    "question": "How much is the amount of the countervailing bond calculated during an investigation?",
    "choices": {
      "A": "Based on the product's market price.",
      "B": "Equal to the provisionally calculated subsidy.",
      "C": "Determined by the Secretary of Trade and Industry",
      "D": "Fixed percentage of the import value."
    },
    "correct": "B",
    "reason": "A countervailing bond is equal to the provisionally calculated subsidy amount."
  },
  "459": {
    "question": "If a farm equipment manufacturer faces competition from subsidized imported machinery, can they request a countervailing investigation?",
    "choices": {
      "A": "No, only consumers can request investigations.",
      "B": "Yes, any interested party can initiate an investigation.",
      "C": "Only if the government approves.",
      "D": "Only if the Secretary of Agriculture recommends it."
    },
    "correct": "B",
    "reason": "Any interested party, including domestic manufacturers, can initiate a countervailing investigation."
  },
  "460": {
    "question": "What is the primary purpose of the Anti-Dumping Act of 1999?",
    "choices": {
      "A": "To promote foreign trade",
      "B": "To protect domestic industries against unfair foreign competition and trade practices",
      "C": "To encourage price competition",
      "D": "To facilitate cross-border investments"
    },
    "correct": "B",
    "reason": "The Anti-Dumping Act of 1999 aims to protect domestic industries from unfair foreign competition."
  },
  "461": {
    "question": "What is the 'normal value' in anti-dumping investigations?",
    "choices": {
      "A": "The price prevailing in the exporting country",
      "B": "The lowest market price",
      "C": "The cost of production",
      "D": "The price set by the domestic industry"
    },
    "correct": "A",
    "reason": "Normal value is the comparable price of the like product in the ordinary course of trade in the exporting country."
  },
  "462": {
    "question": "Which of the following choices is mandated under the provisions of Republic Act 8800?",
    "choices": {
      "A": "The tariff classification of white chocolates imported in boxes in hexing-quadrimeg by the BOC. Said chocolates were not applied for advance classification ruling prior to importation.",
      "B": "There was a sudden surge in the importation of white chocolates from various sources for the past three years. Due to this increased importation the domestic industry producing like products suffered loss in profits.",
      "C": "Exports to the Philippines of bars and rods of steel from a US-based steel industry which was exclusively provided a price support scheme by the US government. Said importation is materially retarding the growth of local steel industry.",
      "D": "A domestic industry manufacturing LPG steel tanks is petitioning the government to increase the MFN import duty rate of steel containers for liquefied gases under Heading 73.11 from the existing 3% to 20% ad valorem."
    },
    "correct": "B",
    "reason": "RA 8800 covers safeguard measures; sudden surge in imports causing injury to domestic industry falls under its provisions."
  },
  "463": {
    "question": "What does the term 'arm's length transaction' refer to in anti-dumping investigations?",
    "choices": {
      "A": "A transaction influenced by buyer-seller relationships",
      "B": "A transaction where price is unaffected by relationships",
      "C": "A transaction involving post-exportation charges",
      "D": "A transaction with government intervention"
    },
    "correct": "B",
    "reason": "Arm's length transaction is one where the price is not affected by any relationship between buyer and seller."
  },
  "464": {
    "question": "What is the key factor in determining material injury caused by dumped imports?",
    "choices": {
      "A": "Volume of dumped imports",
      "B": "Price difference between normal value and export price",
      "C": "Impact on consumers",
      "D": "Exporting country's economic situation"
    },
    "correct": "A",
    "reason": "The volume of dumped imports is a key factor in determining material injury."
  },
  "465": {
    "question": "Under R.A. No. 8800, within how many days from receipt of the Tariff Commission's recommendation shall the Secretary make a decision?",
    "choices": {
      "A": "15 days",
      "B": "15 working days",
      "C": "10 days",
      "D": "10 working days"
    },
    "correct": "A",
    "reason": "The Secretary must make a decision within fifteen (15) days from receipt of the TC recommendation."
  },
  "466": {
    "question": "What is the causal link in anti-dumping investigations?",
    "choices": {
      "A": "The connection between dumping and injury to the domestic industry",
      "B": "The relationship between exporters and importers",
      "C": "The impact of exchange rates on export prices",
      "D": "The correlation between export volume and market demand"
    },
    "correct": "A",
    "reason": "Causal link is the connection between dumping and the resulting injury to the domestic industry."
  },
  "467": {
    "question": "Which of the following choices is not an element of countervailing measures?",
    "choices": {
      "A": "Injury",
      "B": "Like Product",
      "C": "Causal Link",
      "D": "Import Surge"
    },
    "correct": "D",
    "reason": "Import Surge is an element of safeguard measures, not countervailing measures."
  },
  "468": {
    "question": "What is a countervailing bond?",
    "choices": {
      "A": "A bond issued by the exporting country",
      "B": "A security equal to the amount of the provisionally calculated subsidy",
      "C": "A type of export subsidy",
      "D": "A financial guarantee for importers"
    },
    "correct": "B",
    "reason": "A countervailing bond is a security equal to the provisionally calculated subsidy amount."
  },
  "469": {
    "question": "What does the Tariff Commission determine in countervailing cases?",
    "choices": {
      "A": "The amount of subsidy.",
      "B": "The market price of the imported product.",
      "C": "The level of injury to the domestic industry.",
      "D": "The volume of imports."
    },
    "correct": "C",
    "reason": "The Tariff Commission determines the level of injury to the domestic industry in countervailing cases."
  },
  "470": {
    "question": "What is the purpose of the 'lesser duty rule' in anti-dumping investigations?",
    "choices": {
      "A": "To impose the highest possible duty on dumped imports",
      "B": "To limit the duty rate to the minimum necessary to prevent injury",
      "C": "To encourage domestic industries to compete globally",
      "D": "To promote free trade agreements"
    },
    "correct": "B",
    "reason": "The lesser duty rule limits anti-dumping duties to the minimum necessary to prevent injury."
  },
  "471": {
    "question": "Which law provides protection against dumped products in the Philippines?",
    "choices": {
      "A": "Republic Act No. 8800",
      "B": "Republic Act No. 8751",
      "C": "Republic Act No. 8752",
      "D": "Republic Act No. 8753"
    },
    "correct": "C",
    "reason": "Republic Act No. 8752 is the Anti-Dumping Act of 1999."
  },
  "472": {
    "question": "How many days should the Tariff Commission complete its investigation and submit its report to the Secretary from receipt of the referral by the Secretary under R.A. No. 8800?",
    "choices": {
      "A": "60 working days from receipt of the referral",
      "B": "60 days from receipt of the referral",
      "C": "120 working days from receipt of the referral",
      "D": "120 days from receipt of the referral"
    },
    "correct": "D",
    "reason": "Under R.A. No. 8800, the Tariff Commission must complete its formal investigation and submit its report to the Secretary within one hundred twenty (120) calendar days from receipt of the referral (which may be shortened in urgent cases, but 120 days is the standard period)."
  },
  "473": {
    "question": "A country is experiencing an influx of subsidized steel imports. The domestic steel industry claims injury due to these imports. What steps should the government take to address this situation?",
    "choices": {
      "A": "Impose a countervailing duty on all steel imports.",
      "B": "Investigate the existence of subsidies and injury.",
      "C": "Encourage domestic steel producers to reduce prices.",
      "D": "Ignore the issue as it doesn't impact consumers."
    },
    "correct": "B",
    "reason": "The government must investigate the existence of subsidies and injury before imposing countervailing measures."

  "474": {

  "1321": {
    "question": "A foreign vessel engaged in foreign trade is docked at Pier 7, Port of Manila. While the vessel was discharging cargo a container fell on the deck resulting to big damage which necessitates an emergency repair. Since the shipping agent cannot find an appropriate replacement parts for the damaged parts in the Philippines they decided to import the parts. What shall be the treatment for the importation?",
    "choices": {
      "A": "The parts shall enter duty and tax free upon posting of sufficient security for its re-exportation.",
      "B": "The parts shall be subject to CI at the time of importation.",
      "C": "The parts shall enter duty and tax free but the replaced parts must be re-exported.",
      "D": "The parts shall enter duty and tax free."

    "correct": "A"
  },
  "1322": {
    "question": "Which of the following types of conditional importation whose re-exportation period may not be subject to extension?",
    "choices": {

      "C": "Wearing apparels of tourists",
      "D": "Equipment for salvage of vessels or aircrafts"
    },
    "correct": "B"
  },
  "1323": {
    "question": "The item under Section 800 of CMTA that has the longest re-exportation period?",
    "choices": {
      "A": "Equipment for the use in the salvage of vessels and aircrafts",
      "B": "Goods for public exhibition",
      "C": "Trailer chassis imported by freight forwarders",
      "D": "Equipment imported by mining firms"
    },
    "correct": "C"
  },
  "1324": {
    "question": "What shall be presented for unaccompanied personal and household effects of returning resident for purposes of duty/tax exemption?",
    "choices": {
      "A": "Certification of no drawback given.",
      "B": "Affidavit of return to the Philippines",
      "C": "TEI",
      "D": "Export Declaration"
    },
    "correct": "C"
  },
  "1325": {
    "question": "A Filipino Marine General was assigned with the UN Peacekeeping Force Sudan. For him to qualify for duty and tax importation of a vehicle what is the minimum number of years of assignment is required?",
    "choices": {
      "A": "There is no requirement for minimum number of stay because the assignment is dangerous",
      "B": "Not less than 2 years",

      "D": "It depends on the place of assignment and the position level of the Filipino"
    },
    "correct": "D"
  },
  "1326": {
    "question": "Goods for public exhibit were imported under “Temporary Admission” but because of a manmade disaster incurred major damage. Given the facts, how may the “temporary admission” be terminated without re-exportation or payment of duties and taxes?",
    "choices": {
      "A": "The only way to terminate “temporary admission” is to re-export or pay duties and taxes",
      "B": "Condemn the goods for the importer’s account and under customs supervision.",
      "C": "Cancellation of the ATA Carnet by the NIGA.",
      "D": "Request indorsement from the concerned regulatory agency."
    },
    "correct": "B"
  },
  "1327": {
    "question": "As a Customs Broker you were asked by a client of his intention to bring commercial sample which shall be re-exported but the FCA value shall exceed P50,000.00. What may be done for the excess amount?",
    "choices": {
      "A": "The excess amount shall not be allowed entry",
      "B": "The excess amount should be covered by letter of credit to show evidence of payment",
      "C": "The excess amount may be entered for consumption",
      "D": "All of the above"
    },
    "correct": "C"
  },
  "1328": {
    "question": "As a general rule, duties and taxes for goods imported under the provisions of Section 800, CMTA must be paid before they can be used for any other purpose that it was intended to at the time of importation. What is an exception to this rule?",
    "choices": {
      "A": "If the goods imported are not in commercial quantity",
      "B": "If the reason is partition among heirs of the property of a deceased person",
      "C": "If the goods imported are used by reason of emergency",
      "D": "If there is intention of paying the duties and taxes but importer is pressed for time."
    },
    "correct": "B"
  },
  "1329": {
    "question": "Last September 2022 Ambassador “A” was recalled from Cambodia his posting since 2013 and came back with a Toyota Camry duty and tax free. Last March 2023 he was assigned to the United States and again was recalled last June 2025. Can he bring home the Lexus car he was using in US which is registered under his name duty and tax exempt?",
    "choices": {
      "A": "Yes, because he is qualified",
      "B": "Yes, provided that DFA secures approval from the Department of Finance",
      "C": "No, because of EO 156.",
      "D": "No, because he is not qualified under Section 800, CMTA"
    },
    "correct": "D"
  },
  "1330": {
    "question": "The maximum amount of home appliances but one of a kind that an OFW may bring in as a returning resident duty and tax exempt.",
    "choices": {
      "A": "It depends on the number of years that the OFW worked abroad.",
      "B": "P150,000.00 aside from the FCA or FOB value of personal and household effects allowed which depends on the years of stay abroad.",
      "C": "The privilege is included in the FCA or FOB value that may be brought in.",
      "D": "There is no such privilege."
    },
    "correct": "B"
  },
  "1331": {
    "question": "Which of the following is not a requirement by both DOF for purposes of securing TEI or BOC for customs clearance purposes of goods brought into the Philippines for repair, processing or reconditioning?",
    "choices": {
      "A": "Certificate of Identification at the time of entry and re-identification at the time of exportation",
      "B": "Shipping documents",
      "C": "Security equal to 100% of ascertained D&T conditioned to re-exportation within 6 months from acceptance of import entry or payment of D&T",
      "D": "The ATA Carnet shall be cancelled."
    },
    "correct": "C"
  },
  "1332": {
    "question": "What is the maximum amount that qualified Filipinos while abroad may send balikbayan boxes which contain personal and household effects only and are not in commercial quantities intended for barter, sale or for hire?",
    "choices": {
      "A": "One hundred fifty thousand pesos (Php150,000.00)",
      "B": "Seventy five thousand pesos (Php75,000.00) every six months.",
      "C": "Thirty seven thousand pesos (Php37,500.00) every quarter.",
      "D": "Any of the above is proper depending on the qualified Filipino."

    "correct": "A"
  },
  "1333": {
    "question": "What is the re-exportation period of goods belonging to foreign consultants rendering service to the Philippine government that enter conditionally free?",
    "choices": {
      "A": "Three (3) months from acceptance of goods declaration which may be extended for another three (3) months from the expiration of the original period.",
      "B": "It depends on the period of contract of the foreign consultant with the government.",
      "C": "Six (6) months from acceptance of goods declaration which may be extended for another six (6) months from the expiration of the original period.",
      "D": "None of the choices"
    },
    "correct": "A"
  },
  "1334": {
    "question": "In the case of photographic and cinematographic films, undeveloped, exposed outside the Philippines by resident Filipino citizens or by producing companies of Philippine registry where the principal actors and artists are employed for the production are Filipinos upon re-importation may enter conditionally free. Aside from identification what is the other requirement so that the goods may enter conditionally free?",

      "B": "Affidavit by the artists that the exposed films are the same films previously exported from the Philippines.",
      "C": "Affidavit by a disinterested party that the exposed films are the same films previously exported from the Philippines.",
      "D": "Any of the choices is proper"
    },
    "correct": "D"
  },
  "1335": {
    "question": "Machineries, equipment, tools for production, plans to convert mineral ores into saleable form, spare parts, supplies, materials, accessories, explosives, chemicals, and transportation and communications facilities imported by and for the use of new mines and old mines which resume operations may enter conditionally free when certified to as such by which of the following?",
    "choices": {

      "C": "Secretary of the Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR) upon the recommendation of the Chairman, Board of Investments (BOI)",
      "D": "Secretary of the Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR) upon the recommendation of the Director, Mines and Geosciences Bureau (MGB)."
    },
    "correct": "D"
  },
  "1336": {
    "question": "For samples that are not medicines to enter conditionally free a previous authorization must be secured from which of the following?",
    "choices": {
      "A": "Commissioner of Customs",
      "B": "District Collector",
      "C": "Secretary of the Department of Health",
      "D": "Secretary of Finance"
    },
    "correct": "D"
  },

    "question": "How many times may samples of medicines be imported conditionally free for the purpose of introducing new goods in the Philippine market?",

  "1338": {
    "question": "A shipment consisting of household appliances is consigned to the wife of the Ambassador of Qatar to the Philippines. May the appliances enter duty and tax free?",

  "1339": {
    "question": "An equipment was sent abroad for repair after compliance with procedures under Section 800 of CMTA. After repair the equipment was returned to the Philippines through consolidated shipment and covered by a HBL. To repair the equipment some old screws were replaced at a cost of US$100.00, the stand of the equipment was also replaced at a cost of US$200.00 and cost of labor amounted to US$200.00. How shall the customs duty be computed?",
    "choices": {
      "A": "The importation shall be treated as duty free under the provisions of Section 800 of CMTA.",
      "B": "Customs duty shall be imposed based on DV of US$300.00- value of screws and stand and tariff heading to be used is for screws and for stand.",
      "C": "Customs duty shall be imposed based on DV of US$500.00 and tariff heading to be used is for there repaired equipment.",

  "1340": {
    "question": "A shipment consisting of 4X20’ STC Plastic Resins is consigned to Importer “A” who is both an operator of a CBMW and a domestic trader of plastic resins. For this particular shipment the importer would want to have the 2X20’ released simultaneously under goods declaration for consumption with the 2X20’ for warehousing. Is this allowed?",
    "choices": {

  "1341": {
    "question": "For aquatic products to enter duty free the gathering and carrying vessel must be the same. Is the statement correct?",

        "content": "All ports of entry shall be under the supervision and control of a Customs District.             "node_number": "(1)",
            "title": null,
            "content": "Ensure entry of all imported goods at the customs office;",
            "status": "published",
            "version": 1,
            "keywords": [],
            "cross_references": [],
            "notes": [],
            "children": []
          },
          {
            "node_type": "paragraph",
            "node_number": "(2)",
            "title": null,
            "content": "Prevent importation and exportation of prohibited goods;",
            "status": "published",
            "version": 1,
            "keywords": [],
            "cross_references": [],
            "notes": [],
            "children": []
          },
          {
            "node_type": "paragraph",
            "node_number": "(3)",
            "title": null,
            "content": "Ensure legal compliance of regulated goods and facilitate the flow of legitimate trade;",
            "status": "published",
            "version": 1,
            "keywords": [],
            "cross_references": [],
            "notes": [],
            "children": []
          },
          {
            "node_type": "paragraph",
            "node_number": "(4)",
            "title": null,
            "content": "Examine, classify and value imported goods;",
            "status": "published",
            "version": 1,
            "keywords": [],
            "cross_references": [],
            "notes": [],
            "children": []
          },
          {
            "node_type": "paragraph",
            "node_number": "(5)",
            "title": null,
            "content": "Assess and collect duties, taxes and other charges on imported goods;",
            "status": "published",
            "version": 1,
            "keywords": [],
            "cross_references": [],
            "notes": [],
            "children": []
          },
          {
            "node_type": "paragraph",
            "node_number": "(6)",
            "title": null,
            "content": "Hold and dispose imported goods in accordance with this Act;",
            "status": "published",
            "version": 1,
            "keywords": [],
            "cross_references": [],
            "notes": [],
            "children": []
          },
          {
            "node_type": "paragraph",
            "node_number": "(7)",
            "title": null,
            "content": "Prevent smuggling and other customs fraud; and",
            "status": "published",
            "version": 1,
            "keywords": [],
            "cross_references": [],
            "notes": [],
            "children": []
          },
          {
            "node_type": "paragraph",
            "node_number": "(8)",
            "title": null,
            "content": "Perform other necessary duties that may be assigned by the Commissioner for the effective implementation of this Act.",
            "status": "published",
            "version": 1,
            "keywords": [],
            "cross_references": [],
            "notes": [],
            "children": []
          }
        ]
      },
      {
        "node_type": "section",
        "node_number": "211",
        "title": "Temporary Succession of Deputy District Collector to Position of Acting District Collector",
        "content": "In the absence or disability of a District Collector or, in case of vacancy, the Deputy District Collector shall temporarily discharge the duties of the District Collector. Should there be no Deputy District Collector, the District Collector shall designate, in writing, a senior ranking customs officer to temporarily perform the duties of the District Collector. In case there are two (2) or more senior ranking customs officers with equal length of service, a drawing of lots shall be undertaken. The District Collector shall report the designation to the Commissioner within twenty-four (24) hours after the designation.",
        "status": "published",
        "version": 1,
        "keywords": [],
        "cross_references": [],
        "notes": [],
        "children": []
      },
      {
        "node_type": "section",
        "node_number": "212",
        "title": "Records to be Kept by Customs Officers",
        "content": "District Collectors, Deputy District Collectors, and customs officers acting in such capacities must maintain permanent records of official transactions and turn-over all records and official papers to their respective successors or other authorized officials. The records shall be made available for inspection by other authorized officials of the Bureau.\n\nIf required, the District Collector shall affix the official dry seal of the Bureau on all documents and records requiring authentication.",
        "status": "published",
        "version": 1,
        "keywords": [],
        "cross_references": [],
        "notes": [],
        "children": []
      },
      {
        "node_type": "section",
        "node_number": "213",
        "title": "Reports of the District Collector to the Commissioner",
        "content": "The District Collector shall report to the Commissioner any probable or initiated litigation within the Customs District and shall submit regular monthly reports on all district transactions.",
        "status": "published",
        "version": 1,
        "keywords": [],
        "cross_references": [],
        "notes": [],
        "children": []
      }
    ]
  },
  {
    "title_number": "II",
    "title_title": "BUREAU OF CUSTOMS",
    "chapter_number": "3",
    "chapter_title": "EXERCISE OF POLICE AUTHORITY",
    "sections": [
      {
        "node_type": "section",
        "node_number": "214",
        "title": "Persons Exercising Police Authority",
        "content": "For the effective implementation of this Act, the following persons are authorized to effect search, seizure, and arrest:\n\nAll officers authorized by the Commissioner to exercise police authority shall at all times coordinate with the Commissioner.\n\nGoods seized by deputized officers pursuant to this section shall be physically turned-over immediately to the Bureau, unless provided under existing laws, rules and regulations.\n\nFor this purpose, mission orders shall clearly indicate the specific name carrying out the mission and the tasks to be carried out.\n\nSubject to the approval of the Secretary of Finance, the Commissioner shall define the scope, areas covered, procedures and conditions governing the exercise of such police authority including custody and responsibility for the seized goods. The rules and regulations to this effect shall be furnished to the concerned government agencies and personnel for guidance and compliance.\n\nAll seizures pursuant to this section must be effected in accordance with the provisions on the conduct of seizure proceedings provided for in Chapters 3 and 4 of Title XI of this Act.",
        "status": "published",
        "version": 1,
        "keywords": [],
        "cross_references": [
          {
            "reference_text": "CAO No. 10-2020 (Seizure and Forfeiture Proceedings)",
            "url": "https://customs.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/2023/01/CAO-10-2020-Seizure-and-Forfeiture.pdf"
          },
          {
            "reference_text": "CAO No. 03-2019 (Customs Jurisdiction and Police Authority)",
            "url": "https://customs.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/2023/01/cao-03-2019_Customs_Jurisdiction_and_Excercise_of_Police_Authority.pdf"
          }
        ],
        "notes": [],
        "children": [
          {
            "node_type": "paragraph",
            "node_number": "(a)",
            "title": null,
            "content": "Officials of the Bureau, District Collectors, Deputy District Collectors, police officers, agents, inspectors and guards of the Bureau;",
            "status": "published",
            "version": 1,
            "keywords": [],
            "cross_references": [],
            "notes": [],
            "children": []
          },
          {
            "node_type": "paragraph",
            "node_number": "(b)",
            "title": null,
            "content": "Upon authorization of the Commissioner, officers and members of the Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) and national law enforcement agencies; and",
            "status": "published",
            "version": 1,
            "keywords": [],
            "cross_references": [],
            "notes": [],
            "children": []
          },
          {
            "node_type": "paragraph",
            "node_number": "(c)",
            "title": null,
            "content": "Officials of the BIR on all cases falling within the regular performance of their duties, when payment of internal revenue taxes is involved.",
            "status": "published",
            "version": 1,
            "keywords": [],
            "cross_references": [],
            "notes": [],
            "children": []
          }
        ]
      },
      {
        "node_type": "section",
        "node_number": "215",
        "title": "Place Where Authority May be Exercised",
        "content": "All persons exercising police authority as described in the preceding section shall only exercise powers within customs premises as provided for in Section 303 of this Act, and within the limits of the authority granted by the Commissioner.\n\nPort and airport authorities in all ports of entry shall provide authorized customs officers with unhampered access to all premises within their administrative jurisdiction.",
        "status": "published",
        "version": 1,
        "keywords": [],
        "cross_references": [
          "Section 303"
        ],
        "notes": [],
        "children": []
      },
      {
        "node_type": "section",
        "node_number": "216",
        "title": "Exercise of Power of Seizure",
        "content": "Any person exercising police authority under this Act has the power and duty to seize any vessel, aircraft, cargo, goods, animal or any other movable property when the same is subject to forfeiture or when they are subject of a fine imposed under this Act.",
        "status": "published",
        "version": 1,
        "keywords": [],
        "cross_references": [],
        "notes": [],
        "children": []
      },
      {
        "node_type": "section",
        "node_number": "217",
        "title": "Duty of Officer to Disclose Official Character",
        "content": "For the proper exercise of police authority, any authorized person shall disclose the nature of the authority upon being questioned at the time of exercise thereof and shall exhibit the corresponding written authority issued by the Commissioner.",
        "status": "published",
        "version": 1,
        "keywords": [],
        "cross_references": [],
        "notes": [],
        "children": []
      },
      {
        "node_type": "section",
        "node_number": "218",
        "title": "Authority to Require Assistance and Information",
        "content": "Any person exercising police authority may demand the assistance of and request information from the Philippine National Police (PNP), the AFP and other national law enforcement agencies, when necessary, to effect any search, seizure or arrest. It shall be the duty of any police officer and other national law enforcers to give such lawful assistance.",
        "status": "published",
        "version": 1,
        "keywords": [],
        "cross_references": [],
        "notes": [],
        "children": []
      },
      {
        "node_type": "section",
        "node_number": "219",
        "title": "Authority to Enter Properties",
        "content": "Any person exercising police authority may, at any time, enter, pass through, and search any land, enclosure, warehouse, store, building or structure not principally used as a dwelling house.\n\nWhen a security personnel or any other employee lives in the warehouse, store, or any building, structure or enclosure that is used for storage of goods, it shall not be considered as a dwelling house for purposes of this Act.",
        "status": "published",
        "version": 1,
        "keywords": [],
        "cross_references": [],
        "notes": [],
        "children": []
      },
      {
        "node_type": "section",
        "node_number": "220",
        "title": "Authority to Search Dwelling House",
        "content": "A dwelling house may be entered and searched only upon warrant issued by a Judge of a competent court, the sworn application thereupon showing probable cause and particularly describing the place to be searched and the goods to be seized.",
        "status": "published",
        "version": 1,
        "keywords": [],
        "cross_references": [],
        "notes": [],
        "children": []
      },
      {
        "node_type": "section",
        "node_number": "221",
        "title": "Authority to Search Vessels or Aircrafts and Persons or Goods Conveyed Therein",
        "content": "Any person exercising police authority under this Act may board, inspect, search and examine a vessel or aircraft and any container, trunk, package, box or envelope found on board, and physically search and examine any person thereon. In case of any probable violation of this Act, the person exercising police authority may seize the goods, vessel, aircraft, or any part thereof.\n\nSuch power to search includes removal of any false bottom, partition, bulkhead, or any other obstruction for the purpose of uncovering any concealed dutiable or forfeitable goods.\n\nThe proceeding herein authorized shall not give rise to any claim for damage caused to the goods, vessel or aircraft, unless there is gross negligence or abuse of authority in the exercise thereof.",
        "status": "published",
        "version": 1,
        "keywords": [],
        "cross_references": [],
        "notes": [],
        "children": []
      },
      {
        "node_type": "section",
        "node_number": "222",
        "title": "Authority to Search Vehicles, Other Carriers, Persons and Animals",
        "content": "Upon reasonable cause, any person exercising police authority may open and examine any box, trunk, envelope, or other container for purposes of determining the presence of dutiable or prohibited goods. This authority includes the search of receptacles used for the transport of human remains and dead animals. Such authority likewise includes the power to stop, search and examine any vehicle or carrier, person or animal suspected of holding or conveying dutiable or prohibited goods.",
        "status": "published",
        "version": 1,
        "keywords": [],
        "cross_references": [],
        "notes": [],
        "children": []
      },
      {
        "node_type": "section",
        "node_number": "223",
        "title": "Authority to Search Persons Arriving From Foreign Countries",
        "content": "Upon reasonable cause, travelers arriving from foreign countries may be subjected to search and detention by the customs officers. The dignity of the person under search and detention shall be respected at all times. Female inspectors may be employed for the examination and search of persons of their own sex.",
        "status": "published",
        "version": 1,
        "keywords": [],
        "cross_references": [],
        "notes": [],
        "children": []
      },
      {
        "node_type": "section",
        "node_number": "224",
        "title": "Power to Inspect and Visit",
        "content": "The Commissioner or any customs officer who is authorized in writing by the Commissioner, may demand evidence of payment of duties and taxes on imported goods openly for sale or kept in storage. In the event that the interested party fails to produce such evidence within fifteen (15) days, the goods may be seized and subjected to forfeiture proceedings: Provided, That during the proceedings, the interested party shall be given the opportunity to prove or show the source of the goods and the payment of duties and taxes thereon: Provided, further, That when the warrant of seizure has been issued but subsequent documents presented evidencing proper payment are found to be authentic and in order, the District Collector shall, within fifteen (15) days from the receipt of the motion to quash or recall the warrant, cause the immediate release of the goods seized, subject to clearance by the Commissioner: Provided, finally, That the release thereof shall not be contrary to law.",
        "status": "published",
        "version": 1,
        "keywords": [],
        "cross_references": [
          {
            "reference_text": "CMO No. 19-2023 (Customs Districts Workflows for LOA)",
            "url": "https://customs.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/2024-02-OCOM-MEMO.pdf"
          }
        ],
        "notes": [],
        "children": []
      }
    ]
  },
  {
    "title_number": "I",
    "title_title": "TITLE I – PRELIMINARY PROVISIONS",
    "chapter_number": "1",
    "chapter_title": "SHORT TITLE",
    "sections": [
      {
        "node_type": "section",
        "node_number": "100",
        "title": "Short Title",
        "content": "This Act shall be known as the \"Customs Modernization and Tariff Act (CMTA)\".",
        "status": "published",
        "version": 1,
        "keywords": [],
        "cross_references": [
          {
            "reference_text": "Bureau of Customs CMTA Full Text",
            "url": "https://customs.gov.ph"
          }
        ],
        "notes": [],
        "children": []
      }
    ]
  },
  {
    "title_number": "I",
    "title_title": "TITLE I – PRELIMINARY PROVISIONS",
    "chapter_number": "2",
    "chapter_title": "GENERAL AND COMMON PROVISIONS",
    "sections": [
      {
        "node_type": "section",
        "node_number": "101",
        "title": "Declaration of Policy",
        "content": "It is hereby declared the policy of the State to protect and enhance government revenue, institute fair and transparent customs and tariff management that will efficiently facilitate international trade, prevent and curtail any form of customs fraud and illegal acts, and modernize customs and tariff administration. Towards this end, the State shall:",
        "status": "published",
        "version": 1,
        "keywords": [],
        "cross_references": [],
        "notes": [],
        "children": [
          {
            "node_type": "paragraph",
            "node_number": "(a)",
            "title": null,
            "content": "Develop and implement programs for the continuous enhancement of customs systems and processes that will harmonize customs procedures;",
            "status": "published",
            "version": 1,
            "keywords": [],
            "cross_references": [],
            "notes": [],
            "children": []
          },
          {
            "node_type": "paragraph",
            "node_number": "(b)",
            "title": null,
            "content": "Adopt clear and transparent customs rules, regulations, policies and procedures, consistent with international standards and customs best practices;",
            "status": "published",
            "version": 1,
            "keywords": [],
            "cross_references": [],
            "notes": [],
            "children": []
          },
          {
            "node_type": "paragraph",
            "node_number": "(c)",
            "title": null,
            "content": "Establish a regime of transparency and of accessibility to customs information, customs laws, rules, regulations, administrative policies, procedures and practices, in order to ensure informed and diligent compliance with customs practices and procedures by stakeholders;",
            "status": "published",
            "version": 1,
            "keywords": [],
            "cross_references": [],
            "notes": [],
            "children": []
          },
          {
            "node_type": "paragraph",
            "node_number": "(d)",
            "title": null,
            "content": "Consult, coordinate and cooperate with other government agencies and the private sector in implementing and developing customs policy;",
            "status": "published",
            "version": 1,
            "keywords": [],
            "cross_references": [],
            "notes": [],
            "children": []
          },
          {
            "node_type": "paragraph",
            "node_number": "(e)",
            "title": null,
            "content": "Provide a fair and expeditious administrative and judicial appellate remedy for customs related grievances and matters;",
            "status": "published",
            "version": 1,
            "keywords": [],
            "cross_references": [],
            "notes": [],
            "children": []
          },
          {
            "node_type": "paragraph",
            "node_number": "(f)",
            "title": null,
            "content": "Employ modern practices in customs administration and utilize information and communications technology in the implementation of customs functions; and",
            "status": "published",
            "version": 1,
            "keywords": [],
            "cross_references": [],
            "notes": [],
            "children": []
          },
          {
            "node_type": "paragraph",
            "node_number": "(g)",
            "title": null,
            "content": "Institute professionalism and meritocracy in customs tax administration by attracting and retaining competent and capable customs officers and personnel to enforce the provisions of this Act.",
            "status": "published",
            "version": 1,
            "keywords": [],
            "cross_references": [],
            "notes": [],
            "children": []
          }
        ]
      },
      {
        "node_type": "section",
        "node_number": "102",
        "title": "Definition of Terms",
        "content": "As used in this Act:",
        "status": "published",
        "version": 1,
        "keywords": [
          "definitions"
        ],
        "cross_references": [],
        "notes": [],
        "children": [
          {
            "node_type": "paragraph",
            "node_number": "(a) Abatement",
            "title": null,
            "content": "Abatement refers to the reduction or diminution, in whole or in part, of duties and taxes where payment has not been made;",
            "status": "published",
            "version": 1,
            "keywords": [],
            "cross_references": [],
            "notes": [],
            "children": []
          },
          {
            "node_type": "paragraph",
            "node_number": "(b) Actual or Outright Exportation",
            "title": null,
            "content": "Actual or Outright Exportation refers to the customs procedure applicable to goods which, being in free circulation, leave the Philippine territory and are intended to remain permanently outside it;",
            "status": "published",
            "version": 1,
            "keywords": [],
            "cross_references": [],
            "notes": [],
            "children": []
          },
          {
            "node_type": "paragraph",
            "node_number": "(c) Admission",
            "title": null,
            "content": "Admission refers to the act of bringing imported goods directly or through transit into a free zone;",
            "status": "published",
            "version": 1,
            "keywords": [],
            "cross_references": [],
            "notes": [],
            "children": []
          },
          {
            "node_type": "paragraph",
            "node_number": "(d) Airway Bill (AWB)",
            "title": null,
            "content": "Airway Bill (AWB) refers to a transport document for airfreight used by airlines and international freight forwarders which specify the holder or consignee of the bill who has the right to claim delivery of the goods when they arrive at the port of destination. It is a contract of carriage that includes carrier conditions, such as limits of liability and claims procedures. In addition, it contains transport instructions to airlines and carriers, a description of the goods, and applicable transportation charges;",
            "status": "published",
            "version": 1,
            "keywords": [],
            "cross_references": [],
            "notes": [],
            "children": []
          },
          {
            "node_type": "paragraph",
            "node_number": "(e) Appeal",
            "title": null,
            "content": "Appeal refers to the remedy by which a person who is aggrieved or adversely affected by any action, decision, order, or omission of the Bureau, seeks redress before the Bureau, the Secretary of Finance, or competent court, as the case may be;",
            "status": "published",
            "version": 1,
            "keywords": [],
            "cross_references": [],
            "notes": [],
            "children": []
          },
          {
            "node_type": "paragraph",
            "node_number": "(f) Assessment",
            "title": null,
            "content": "Assessment refers to the process of determining the amount of duties and taxes and other charges due on imported and exported goods;",
            "status": "published",
            "version": 1,
            "keywords": [],
            "cross_references": [],
            "notes": [],
            "children": []
          },
          {
            "node_type": "paragraph",
            "node_number": "(g) Authorized Economic Operator (AEO)",
            "title": null,
            "content": "Authorized Economic Operator (AEO) refers to the importer, exporter, customs broker, forwarder, freight forwarder, transport provider, and any other entity duly accredited by the Bureau based on the World Customs Organization (WCO) Framework of Standards to Secure and Facilitate Global Trade, the Revised Kyoto Convention (RKC), the WCO Supply Chain Management Guidelines and the various national best practices to promote trade facilitation and to provide a seamless movement of goods across borders through secure international trade supply chains with the use of risk management and modern technology;",
            "status": "published",
            "version": 1,
            "keywords": [],
            "cross_references": [],
            "notes": [],
            "children": []
          },
          {
            "node_type": "paragraph",
            "node_number": "(h) Bill of Lading (B/L)",
            "title": null,
            "content": "Bill of Lading (B/L) refers to a transport document issued by shipping lines, carriers and international freight forwarders or non-vessel operating common carrier for water-borne freight. The holder or consignee of the bill has the right to claim delivery of the goods at the port of destination. It is a contract of carriage that includes carrier conditions, such as limits of liability and claims procedures. In addition, it contains transport instructions to shipping lines and carriers, a description of the goods, and applicable transportation charges;",
            "status": "published",
            "version": 1,
            "keywords": [],
            "cross_references": [],
            "notes": [],
            "children": []
          },
          {
            "node_type": "paragraph",
            "node_number": "(i) Bureau",
            "title": null,
            "content": "Bureau refers to the Bureau of Customs;",
            "status": "published",
            "version": 1,
            "keywords": [],
            "cross_references": [],
            "notes": [],
            "children": []
          },
          {
            "node_type": "paragraph",
            "node_number": "(j) Carrier",
            "title": null,
            "content": "Carrier refers to the person actually transporting goods or in charge of or responsible for the operation of the means of transport such as airlines, shipping lines, freight forwarders, cargo consolidators, non-vessel operating common carriers and other international transport operators;",
            "status": "published",
            "version": 1,
            "keywords": [],
            "cross_references": [],
            "notes": [],
            "children": []
          },
          {
            "node_type": "paragraph",
            "node_number": "(k) Clearance",
            "title": null,
            "content": "Clearance refers to the completion of customs and other government formalities necessary to allow goods to enter for consumption, warehousing, transit or transshipment, or to be exported or placed under another customs procedure;",
            "status": "published",
            "version": 1,
            "keywords": [],
            "cross_references": [],
            "notes": [],
            "children": []
          },
          {
            "node_type": "paragraph",
            "node_number": "(l) Commission",
            "title": null,
            "content": "Commission refers to the Tariff Commission;",
            "status": "published",
            "version": 1,
            "keywords": [],
            "cross_references": [],
            "notes": [],
            "children": []
          },
          {
            "node_type": "paragraph",
            "node_number": "(m) Conditional Importation",
            "title": null,
            "content": "Conditional Importation refers to the customs procedure known under the RKC as temporary admission in which certain goods can be brought into a customs territory conditionally relieved, totally or partially, from payment of import duties and taxes; such goods must be imported for a specific purpose and must be intended for reexportation within a specified period and without having undergone any substantial change except due to normal depreciation;",
            "status": "published",
            "version": 1,
            "keywords": [],
            "cross_references": [],
            "notes": [],
            "children": []
          },
          {
            "node_type": "paragraph",
            "node_number": "(n) Customs Broker",
            "title": null,
            "content": "Customs Broker refers to any person who is a bona fide holder of a valid Certificate of Registration/Professional Identification Card issued by the Professional Regulatory Board and Professional Regulation Commission pursuant to Republic Act No. 9280, as amended, otherwise known as the \"Customs Brokers Act of 2004\";",
            "status": "published",
            "version": 1,
            "keywords": [],
            "cross_references": [],
            "notes": [],
            "children": []
          },
          {
            "node_type": "paragraph",
            "node_number": "(o) Customs Office",
            "title": null,
            "content": "Customs Office refers to any customs administrative unit that is competent and authorized to perform all or any of the functions enumerated under customs and tariff laws;",
            "status": "published",
            "version": 1,
            "keywords": [],
            "cross_references": [],
            "notes": [],
            "children": []
          },
          {
            "node_type": "paragraph",
            "node_number": "(p) Customs Officer",
            "title": null,
            "content": "Customs Officer, as distinguished from a clerk or employee, refers to a person whose duty, not being clerical or manual in nature, involves the exercise of discretion in performing the function of the Bureau. It may also refer to an employee authorized to perform a specific function of the Bureau as provided in this Act;",
            "status": "published",
            "version": 1,
            "keywords": [],
            "cross_references": [],
            "notes": [],
            "children": []
          },
          {
            "node_type": "paragraph",
            "node_number": "(q) Customs Territory",
            "title": null,
            "content": "Customs Territory refers to areas in the Philippines where customs and tariff laws may be enforced;",
            "status": "published",
            "version": 1,
            "keywords": [],
            "cross_references": [],
            "notes": [],
            "children": []
          },
          {
            "node_type": "paragraph",
            "node_number": "(r) Entry",
            "title": null,
            "content": "Entry refers to the act, documentation and process of bringing imported goods into the customs territory, including goods coming from free zones;",
            "status": "published",
            "version": 1,
            "keywords": [],
            "cross_references": [],
            "notes": [],
            "children": []
          },
          {
            "node_type": "paragraph",
            "node_number": "(s) Exportation",
            "title": null,
            "content": "Exportation refers to the act, documentation, and process of bringing goods out of Philippine territory;",
            "status": "published",
            "version": 1,
            "keywords": [],
            "cross_references": [],
            "notes": [],
            "children": []
          },
          {
            "node_type": "paragraph",
            "node_number": "(t) Export Declaration",
            "title": null,
            "content": "Export Declaration refers to a statement made in the manner prescribed by the Bureau and other appropriate agencies, by which the persons concerned indicate the procedure to be observed for taking out or causing to be taken out any exported goods and the particulars of which the customs administration shall require;",
            "status": "published",
            "version": 1,
            "keywords": [],
            "cross_references": [],
            "notes": [],
            "children": []
          },
          {
            "node_type": "paragraph",
            "node_number": "(u) Flexible Clause",
            "title": null,
            "content": "Flexible Clause refer to the power of the President upon recommendation of the National Economic and Development Authority (NEDA): (1) to increase, reduce or remove existing protective tariff rates of import duty, but in no case shall be higher than one hundred percent (100%) ad valorem; (2) to establish import quota or to ban importation of any commodity as may be necessary; and (3) to impose additional duty on all import not exceeding ten percent (10%) ad valorem, whenever necessary;",
            "status": "published",
            "version": 1,
            "keywords": [],
            "cross_references": [],
            "notes": [],
            "children": []
          },
          {
            "node_type": "paragraph",
            "node_number": "(v) Foreign Exporter",
            "title": null,
            "content": "Foreign Exporter refers to one whose name appears on documentation attesting to the export of the product to the Philippines regardless of the manufacturer's name in the invoice;",
            "status": "published",
            "version": 1,
            "keywords": [],
            "cross_references": [],
            "notes": [],
            "children": []
          },
          {
            "node_type": "paragraph",
            "node_number": "(w) Free Zone",
            "title": null,
            "content": "Free Zone refers to special economic zones registered with the Philippine Economic Zone Authority (PEZA) under Republic Act No. 7916, as amended, duly chartered or legislated special economic zones and freeports such as Clark Freeport Zone, Poro Point Freeport Zone, John Hay Special Economic Zone and Subic Bay Freeport Zone under Republic Act No. 7227, as amended by Republic Act No. 9400; the Aurora Special Economic Zone under Republic Act No. 9490, as amended; the Cagayan Special Economic Zone and Freeport under Republic Act No. 7922; the Zamboanga City Special Economic Zone under Republic Act No. 7903; the Freeport Area of Bataan under Republic Act No. 9728; and such other freeports as established or may be created by law;",
            "status": "published",
            "version": 1,
            "keywords": [],
            "cross_references": [],
            "notes": [],
            "children": []
          },
          {
            "node_type": "paragraph",
            "node_number": "(x) Goods",
            "title": null,
            "content": "Goods refer to articles, wares, merchandise and any other items which are subject of importation or exportation;",
            "status": "published",
            "version": 1,
            "keywords": [],
            "cross_references": [],
            "notes": [],
            "children": []
          },
          {
            "node_type": "paragraph",
            "node_number": "(y) Goods Declaration",
            "title": null,
            "content": "Goods Declaration refers to a statement made in the manner prescribed by the Bureau and other appropriate agencies, by which the persons concerned indicate the procedure to be observed in the application for the entry or admission of imported goods and the particulars of which the customs administration shall require;",
            "status": "published",
            "version": 1,
            "keywords": [],
            "cross_references": [],
            "notes": [],
            "children": []
          },
          {
            "node_type": "paragraph",
            "node_number": "(z) Importation",
            "title": null,
            "content": "Importation refers to the act of bringing in of goods from a foreign territory into Philippine territory, whether for consumption, warehousing, or admission as defined in this Act;",
            "status": "published",
            "version": 1,
            "keywords": [],
            "cross_references": [],
            "notes": [],
            "children": []
          },
          {
            "node_type": "paragraph",
            "node_number": "(aa) Freight Forwarder",
            "title": null,
            "content": "Freight Forwarder refers to a local entity that acts as a cargo intermediary and facilitates transport of goods on behalf of its client without assuming the role of a carrier, which can also perform other forwarding services, such as booking cargo space, negotiating freight rates, preparing documents, advancing freight payments, providing packing/crating, trucking and warehousing, engaging as an agent/representative of a foreign non-vessel operating as a common carrier/cargo consolidator named in a master bill of lading as consignee of a consolidated shipment, and other related undertakings;",
            "status": "published",
            "version": 1,
            "keywords": [],
            "cross_references": [],
            "notes": [],
            "children": []
          },
          {
            "node_type": "paragraph",
            "node_number": "(bb) International Freight Forwarder",
            "title": null,
            "content": "International Freight Forwarder refers to persons responsible for the assembly and consolidation of shipments into single lot, and assuming, in most cases, the full responsibility for the international transport of such shipment from point of receipt to the point of destination;",
            "status": "published",
            "version": 1,
            "keywords": [],
            "cross_references": [],
            "notes": [],
            "children": []
          },
          {
            "node_type": "paragraph",
            "node_number": "(cc) Jurisdictional Control",
            "title": null,
            "content": "Jurisdictional Control refers to the power and rights of the Bureau in exercising supervision and police authority over all seas within the jurisdiction of the Philippine territory and over all coasts, ports, airports, harbors, bays, rivers and inland waters whether navigable or not from the sea;",
            "status": "published",
            "version": 1,
            "keywords": [],
            "cross_references": [],
            "notes": [],
            "children": []
          },
          {
            "node_type": "paragraph",
            "node_number": "(dd) Lodgement",
            "title": null,
            "content": "Lodgement refers to the registration of a goods declaration with the Bureau;",
            "status": "published",
            "version": 1,
            "keywords": [],
            "cross_references": [],
            "notes": [],
            "children": []
          },
          {
            "node_type": "paragraph",
            "node_number": "(ee) Non-Vessel Operating Common Carrier (NVOCC)",
            "title": null,
            "content": "Non-Vessel Operating Common Carrier (NVOCC) refers to an entity, which may or may not own or operate a vessel that provides a point-to-point service which may include several modes of transport and/or undertakes group age of less container load (LCL) shipments and issues the corresponding transport document;",
            "status": "published",
            "version": 1,
            "keywords": [],
            "cross_references": [],
            "notes": [],
            "children": []
          },
          {
            "node_type": "paragraph",
            "node_number": "(ff) Outright Smuggling",
            "title": null,
            "content": "Outright Smuggling refers to an act of importing goods into the country without complete customs prescribed importation documents, or without being cleared by customs or other regulatory government agencies, for the purpose of evading payment of prescribed taxes, duties and other government charges;",
            "status": "published",
            "version": 1,
            "keywords": [],
            "cross_references": [],
            "notes": [],
            "children": []
          },
          {
            "node_type": "paragraph",
            "node_number": "(gg) Perishable Good",
            "title": null,
            "content": "Perishable Good refers to goods liable to perish or goods that depreciate greatly in value while stored or which cannot be kept without great disproportionate expense, which may be proceeded to, advertised and sold at auction upon notice if deemed reasonable;",
            "status": "published",
            "version": 1,
            "keywords": [],
            "cross_references": [],
            "notes": [],
            "children": []
          },
          {
            "node_type": "paragraph",
            "node_number": "(hh) Port of Entry",
            "title": null,
            "content": "Port of Entry refers to a domestic port open to both domestic and international trade, including principal ports of entry and subports of entry. A principal port of entry is the chiefport of entry of the Customs District wherein it is situated and is the permanent station of the District Collector of such port. Subports of entry are under the administrative jurisdiction of the District Collector of the principal port of entry of the Customs District. Port of entry as used in this Act shall include airport of entry;",
            "status": "published",
            "version": 1,
            "keywords": [],
            "cross_references": [],
            "notes": [],
            "children": []
          },
          {
            "node_type": "paragraph",
            "node_number": "(ii) Port of Discharge",
            "title": null,
            "content": "Port of Discharge, also called Port of Unloading, refers to a place where a vessel, ship, aircraft or train unloads its shipments, from where they will be dispatched to their respective consignees;",
            "status": "published",
            "version": 1,
            "keywords": [],
            "cross_references": [],
            "notes": [],
            "children": []
          },
          {
            "node_type": "paragraph",
            "node_number": "(jj) Reexportation",
            "title": null,
            "content": "Reexportation means exportation of goods which have been imported;",
            "status": "published",
            "version": 1,
            "keywords": [],
            "cross_references": [],
            "notes": [],
            "children": []
          },
          {
            "node_type": "paragraph",
            "node_number": "(kk) Release of Goods",
            "title": null,
            "content": "Release of Goods refers to the action by the Bureau to permit goods undergoing clearance to be placed at the disposal of the party concerned;",
            "status": "published",
            "version": 1,
            "keywords": [],
            "cross_references": [],
            "notes": [],
            "children": []
          },
          {
            "node_type": "paragraph",
            "node_number": "(ll) Refund",
            "title": null,
            "content": "Refund refers to the return, in whole or in part, of duties and taxes paid on goods;",
            "status": "published",
            "version": 1,
            "keywords": [],
            "cross_references": [],
            "notes": [],
            "children": []
          },
          {
            "node_type": "paragraph",
            "node_number": "(mm) Security",
            "title": null,
            "content": "Security refers to any form of guaranty, such as a surety bond, cash bond, standby letter of credit or irrevocable letter of credit, which ensures the satisfaction of an obligation to the Bureau;",
            "status": "published",
            "version": 1,
            "keywords": [],
            "cross_references": [],
            "notes": [],
            "children": []
          },
          {
            "node_type": "paragraph",
            "node_number": "(nn) Smuggling",
            "title": null,
            "content": "Smuggling refers to the fraudulent act of importing any goods into the Philippines, or the act of assisting in receiving, concealing, buying, selling, disposing or transporting such goods, with full knowledge that the same has been fraudulently imported, or the fraudulent exportation of goods. Goods referred to under this definition shall be known as smuggled goods;",
            "status": "published",
            "version": 1,
            "keywords": [],
            "cross_references": [],
            "notes": [],
            "children": []
          },
          {
            "node_type": "paragraph",
            "node_number": "(oo) Taxes",
            "title": null,
            "content": "Taxes refer to all taxes, fees and charges imposed under this Act and the National Internal Revenue Code (NIRC) of 1997, as amended, and collected by the Bureau;",
            "status": "published",
            "version": 1,
            "keywords": [],
            "cross_references": [],
            "notes": [],
            "children": []
          },
          {
            "node_type": "paragraph",
            "node_number": "(pp) Technical Smuggling",
            "title": null,
            "content": "Technical Smuggling refers to the act of importing goods into the country by means of fraudulent, falsified or erroneous declaration of the goods to its nature, kind, quality, quantity or weight, for the purpose of reducing or avoiding payment of prescribed taxes, duties and other charges;",
            "status": "published",
            "version": 1,
            "keywords": [],
            "cross_references": [],
            "notes": [],
            "children": []
          },
          {
            "node_type": "paragraph",
            "node_number": "(qq) Tentative Release",
            "title": null,
            "content": "Tentative Release refers to a case where the assessment is disputed and pending review, an importer may put up a cash bond equivalent to the duties and taxes due on goods before the importer can obtain the release of said goods;",
            "status": "published",
            "version": 1,
            "keywords": [],
            "cross_references": [],
            "notes": [],
            "children": []
          },
          {
            "node_type": "paragraph",
            "node_number": "(rr) Transit",
            "title": null,
            "content": "Transit refers to the customs procedure under which goods, in its original form, are transported under customs control from one customs office to another, or to a free zone;",
            "status": "published",
            "version": 1,
            "keywords": [],
            "cross_references": [],
            "notes": [],
            "children": []
          },
          {
            "node_type": "paragraph",
            "node_number": "(ss) Transshipment",
            "title": null,
            "content": "Transshipment refers to the customs procedure under which goods are transferred under customs control from the importing means of transport to the exporting means of transport within the area of one customs office, which is the office of both importation and exportation;",
            "status": "published",
            "version": 1,
            "keywords": [],
            "cross_references": [],
            "notes": [],
